# Instructions

## Pre-modification Steps

Refer “[Anonymized Customer]” to integrate PaaS (VBCS) application in SaaS. ## Modify PaaS application integration

- Login to Fusion
- In home page, on top right hand side click on UserName icon and select “Setup and Maintenance” item from drop down menu. - Then select “Manage Setup content” task from Task List available on right hand side of page. - Then select “Manage Integration of Additional Application”. - It will navigate to “Manage Integration of Additional Application” page. In this page select  “[Anonymized Customer]” application and click on edit option. - In edit Application Integration page, replace existing Full URL with new one. In our case the existing URL is referring to PROD environment which is below
https://[Anonymized Customer]-oraclecloudinteg.integration.ocp.oraclecloud.com/ic/builder/rt/[Anonymized Customer]/live

# Introduction

## Purpose

[Anonymized Customer] Novus Project will implement a single Oracle SaaS platform for Finance and Supply Chain across the [Anonymized Customer] Group. The purpose of this document is to provide a High-Level Global Design for the Novus Project. “Global” shall mean a single common system design for the Oracle Cloud applications, for adoption by Group Entities in all regions. “Localizations” shall mean parts of the design that are local to a specific site for local statutory or legal reasons. The relationship of this document to other items within the whole end-to-end solution of the Novus Project can be summarized in the Enterprise Architecture context diagram below. This document should be taken as a Master Document for referring to detailed design documents that constitute the whole design. Additional supporting documents should be referenced in Appendix A. This document has been created to deliver the Global Design for all [Anonymized Customer] legal entities based on the Novus project design principles and adopting an Oracle Cloud SaaS solution at the time of the Global Design and validation phases of the Novus project. Following the implementation of the pilot sites in the Benelux Sales Channels and DLG Manufacturing, during the rollout to other [Anonymized Customer] entities, design decisions and processes may evolve whether globally or have local exceptions. In additional new release features and Oracle cloud services, licensed not yet implemented, may be deployed. ## Design Principles

The Novus project design principles the global design aligns to are:

---
**Table:**

| 1 | Process harmonization | Process harmonization is a key driver. Wherever possible, we need to agree consistent processes and policies for all activities. |
| 2 | Customer Experience | One process, with little exceptions. This brings consistency of our customers and customer facing teams. We need to modernize our systems for a superior customer life-time experience. |
| 3 | Simplify and streamline | Strive for a seamless process We need to breakdown ‘walls’ between our systems. Leverage features from our new business system tools to allow for value-add activities. |
| 4 | Adopt system defined processes | Adopt system-defined processes to align with best practice where possible. We need to avoid processes that drive system customizations.

|
| 5 | Avoid working outside of core systems | We need to eliminate spreadsheets and manual work whenever possible. |
| 6 | Automate processes | Starts with proper design and has the customer in mind. We must get to a point where we understand the complete end-to-end process and mitigate weak points. |
| 7 | Do it once, do it right | Reduce the number of human driven choices. We must enforce data discipline and drive data quality. |
| 8 | Consider the user experience | Allow self-service on a device and at time that suits them. We need to consider how users’ interface with [Anonymized Customer] through our business systems.

|

## Enterprise Structures

Every enterprise has three fundamental structures: legal, managerial, and functional, that are used to describe its operation and provide a basis for reporting. In Oracle Cloud, these structures are implemented using the chart of accounts and enterprise organization structure. The following diagrams represent the Enterprise Structure that will be implemented for [Anonymized Customer]. This includes Ledgers, Legal Entities, Business Units, and Inventory Organizations. ## UK and Europe

Americas, Canada, Mexico, UAE

## Asia Pacific

### Enterprise

The name of the Enterprise will be ‘[Anonymized Customer] Group’. Note: this does not drive any reporting. ### Ledgers

Ledger is the Oracle Cloud enterprise structure that configures, manages, and secures journals and financial balances of the main bookkeeping entity.

It is where transaction balances are recorded against a Chart of accounts, Calendar and Currency and accounting Convention. [Anonymized Customer] will have One Primary Ledger for each country in the local currency. The following will be common across [Anonymized Customer] Primary Ledgers:
- Chart of Accounts
- Accounting Method
- Accounting Calendar

### Secondary Ledgers

### A secondary ledger is an optional ledger linked to a primary ledger. A secondary ledger can differ from its related primary ledger in Chart of accounts, Calendar, Currency, accounting Convention, or ledger processing options. Reporting requirements, for example, that require a different accounting representation to comply with international or country-specific regulations, create the need for a secondary ledger. ### The following Countries will require secondary ledgers: China (Statutory Calendar); Spain (Statutory COA); France (Statutory COA); Portugal (Statutory COA & Calendar); Mexico (Statutory COA & Calendar). A secondary ledger for each of these will be defined with the COA structure for local regulatory reporting where applicable. Please refer to the Chart of Accounts design book for Global Design. ### Reporting Currency Ledgers

### Reporting currencies are the currency used for financial, legal, and management reporting. If the reporting currency is not the same as the ledger currency, the foreign currency translation process or reporting currencies functionality can be used to convert the ledger account balances in a reporting currency. Currency conversion rules are required to instruct the system on how to convert the transactions, journals, or balances from the source representation to the reporting currency. A reporting ledger (GBP) will be deployed for Dubai to support consolidation with DUK. A reporting ledger (USD) will be deployed for Mexico to support group management reporting. ### Consolidation Ledgers

An optional ‘primary’ ledger used to sum values for specified entities from multiple ledgers:
Shares same chart of accounts, calendar, accounting method & currency
Is trans-national
Multiple consolidation ledgers can be created
Note: Consolidation ledgers are usually used for straightforward consolidations
There are no requirements to use consolidation ledgers for [Anonymized Customer]. Consolidation processes will be performed in [Anonymized Customer]’s IBM Planning Analytics (Cognos) application.

### Legal Entities

A legal entity is a real-world entity that may enter into agreements or contracts, assume obligations, incur, and pay debts, sue, and be sued, and be held responsible for its actions. In the context of Procurement and Financials, the legal entity is responsible for paying and collecting transaction-based taxes; submitting detailed transaction and accounting reports to the authorities; and complying with local regulations applicable to financial processing and reporting. Only true legal entities and branches will be created as Legal Entities in Oracle. Each entity will be represented by a single primary Balancing Segment Value. ### Finance and SCM Business Units

An Oracle business unit is an Oracle Cloud enterprise structure that administers and secures subledger transactions such as sales orders, invoices, payments, and cash receipts. Oracle business units may be responsible for performing one or more business functions such as Requisitioning, Payables Invoicing, Payables Payments and Billing and Revenue Management.

There must be at least one Oracle Business Unit for each ledger that utilizes subledgers, and business units cannot span multiple ledgers. All appropriate Finance and SCM Business Functions will be assigned to one Business Unit. Appropriate simply refers to not all Business Units may have the same functions. There will be a 1:1 relationship between a business unit and legal entity with a few exceptions, e.g., [Anonymized Customer] UK Limited will have 1: Many. This is reflected in the diagrams. ### Procurement Business Units

Procurement business functions will be modelled within one Global Procurement Business Unit. This business unit will master supplier relationships, supplier agreements and enable [Anonymized Customer] to monitor supplier spend across all legal entities. A relationship will be modelled between the requisitioning business units (other Legal Entities) and the Global Procurement Business Unit. Contracts and suppliers will be created in the Global Procurement Business Unit and assigned to the relevant requisitioning business units. All purchase requisitions raised in the individual Legal Entities will be converted to purchase orders in the Global Procurement Unit. This will [Anonymized Customer] having an enterprise view of suppliers, contracts and purchase order spend. ### Inventory Organizations

## Item Master Organization

An item master organization lists and describes items that are shared across several inventory organizations or item organizations. The master organization serves as a data repository storing items and item attributes, master level categories and category sets, master level cross references, and numerous data defaults. [Anonymized Customer] will have a single, global item master organization. Item Organization
An item organization defines an item when inventory balances aren't stored, and inventory storage or inventory movement isn't reflected in Oracle Cloud Applications. There will be an EU Validation Item Organization, which will also be used by the UK channels. Other Validation Item Organizations are yet to be decided to support other regions, e.g. US and Asia–Pacific. The key design principle is as few validation organizations as possible. Inventory Organization
In Oracle Cloud, storage facilities, warehouses, and distribution centres are implemented as inventory organizations. A logical or physical entity in the enterprise that is used to store definitions of items or store and transact items.

Each Sales Channel will have the following inventory organizations:
1 x S (Service) Organization
At least 1 x W (Warehouse) Organization depending on the number of warehouses / locations
1 x L (Loan) Organization
- Note: UK Distribution and SG Sales Channel are distribution channels and will not have these organizations. - Each Manufacturing site will have the following inventory organizations:
1 x M (Manufacturing) Organization for each manufacturing location
Manufacturing and maintenance will be managed in the same inventory organization. 1 x L (Loan) Organization
Manufacturing sites will not maintain Hire and Demo stock; however, the Loan Organizations can be used to support processes such as loan stock being returned to the site. 1 x R (R&D) Organization
- A Manufacturing site may have a S (Service) Organization. Currently, only [Anonymized Customer] Laser Gmbh (DLG) uses a Service Organization. - Hub Organizations:
There are three Hub organizations that will be configured where stock is consolidated in a warehouse for distribution to the local country sites. The current hub organizations are in Spain and Netherlands owned by the UK and one in Canada owned by [Anonymized Customer] Printing Solutions Inc. Cost Organization
Cost Organizations represent the level at which Costing can be secured, linked to a Legal Entity, and “contains” one or more Inventory Organizations, all belonging to a single Profit Center Business Unit (PCBU). There will be one Cost Organization per PCBU. A single cost method, Standard Cost, will be used for all transactions. Note: Local Regulatory requirements may require some Business Units to use Average Costing in their Cost Organization, e.g., Mexico. ### Legal Employers

All legal entities will be Legal Employers, i.e., employs people within that legal entity. Legal Employers to employee mapping are maintained in [Anonymized Customer]’s HCM system – Sage Connect and the assignment of Legal Employers to Employees in Oracle Cloud will mirror this. ### Reference Data Sets

# Introduction

## Purpose

The objective of this document is to provide a Technical Specification to:
Establish a functional design to address key business objectives. Provide traceability between business requirements and the delivered components. Identify the touchpoints for any functional level integration. Capture any key dependencies. Provide high level functional design for [Anonymized Customer] ERP Leads and Technical Leads to confirm what will be delivered. Provide the necessary information with enough detail so that the technical teams, and/or external 3rd parties, have a clear understanding of the functional requirements that will enable them to design and build the extension component to satisfy the requirements. Assist the testing teams in understanding what to test. ## Scope

This document specifies the business context, requirements, dependencies, and technical considerations for the technical team for the development & configuration for CR077c- Fusion Exchange Rates to GTM Integration. ## Overview

Operating and continuing to actively maintain a Trade Compliance program is a vital component of doing business in the modern and constantly changing landscape of global trade. An effective program seeks to ensure adherence to all relevant trade regulations in all operating countries, and ultimately to protect and avoid companies being exposed to risk that can include delays, penalties, and even loss of trade privileges. Compliance programs should include clearly defined processes and procedures for screening customers and vendors, reviewing all shipments, ensuring compliance with applicable government sanctions, applying for licenses to export or import goods, checking business is not conducted with third parties in embargoed countries, and generally ensuring that all requirements (regulatory and also those driven by company policy) are met regarding exports and imports.

Additionally, all compliance programs must recognize that new regulations can be introduced, or change, at any time and therefore procedures and even processes should be subject to continual review and update to meet the latest requirements and ensure accurate and auditable records are maintained for all business transactions. To facilitate this compliance program, GTM will be deployed by [Anonymized Customer] to initially cover the business areas of Benelux and Germany. This integration design will cover the data and process required for integrating Exchange Rates from Oracle Fusion Cloud to Oracle Global Trade Management Cloud for use in the FTA Qualification process. # Business Objectives

## Process Overview

As part of the configurations required to perform FTA Qualification calculations within GTM, the Fusion Exchange Rates must be loaded into GTM to be used in any currency conversions that are required. All Exchange Rates that exist in Fusion must be maintained in GTM by sending the data into the system via an integration as follows:

### Assumptions

The following key assumptions are required to support this design. - Exchange rates that are entered in Oracle Fusion shall be picked for this Integration
- Only Corporate Rate Type will be picked
- Last Run Date shall be captured in ATP Table xxdom_exchange_rate_lookup, column LastRunDateTime. ### High Level Approach

- Integration “XxLoadFusionExchangeRateToGTM” will be a scheduled integration which will extract Exchange Rates defined in Fusion and shall load to GTM
- Integration shall invoke Fusion BI Report Service to invoke and extract data from a BIP Report. - BIP Report shall extract Fusion Exchange Rate created or updated from last run data time. - Integration shall invoke OIC Logistics Adapter GTM Exchange Rate service to send the Exchange Rate to GTM

# Introduction

## Purpose

The objective of this document is to provide a Technical Specification to:
Establish a functional design to address key business objectives. Provide traceability between business requirements and the delivered components. Identify the touchpoints for any functional level integration. Capture any key dependencies. Provide high level functional design for [Anonymized Customer] ERP Leads and Technical Leads to confirm what will be delivered. Provide the necessary information with enough detail so that the technical teams, and/or external 3rd parties, have a clear understanding of the functional requirements that will enable them to design and build the extension component to satisfy the requirements. Assist the testing teams in understanding what to test. ## Scope

This document specifies the business context, requirements, dependencies, and technical considerations for the technical team for the development & configuration for CR077c- Fusion Exchange Rates to GTM Integration. ## Overview

Operating and continuing to actively maintain a Trade Compliance program is a vital component of doing business in the modern and constantly changing landscape of global trade. An effective program seeks to ensure adherence to all relevant trade regulations in all operating countries, and ultimately to protect and avoid companies being exposed to risk that can include delays, penalties, and even loss of trade privileges. Compliance programs should include clearly defined processes and procedures for screening customers and vendors, reviewing all shipments, ensuring compliance with applicable government sanctions, applying for licenses to export or import goods, checking business is not conducted with third parties in embargoed countries, and generally ensuring that all requirements (regulatory and also those driven by company policy) are met regarding exports and imports.

Additionally, all compliance programs must recognize that new regulations can be introduced, or change, at any time and therefore procedures and even processes should be subject to continual review and update to meet the latest requirements and ensure accurate and auditable records are maintained for all business transactions. To facilitate this compliance program, GTM will be deployed by [Anonymized Customer] to initially cover the business areas of Benelux and Germany. This integration design will cover the data and process required for integrating Exchange Rates from Oracle Fusion Cloud to Oracle Global Trade Management Cloud for use in the FTA Qualification process. # Business Objectives

## Process Overview

As part of the configurations required to perform FTA Qualification calculations within GTM, the Fusion Exchange Rates must be loaded into GTM to be used in any currency conversions that are required. All Exchange Rates that exist in Fusion must be maintained in GTM by sending the data into the system via an integration as follows:

# Introduction

## Purpose

This Design Specification documents the detailed design updating ABC Classification on a given Item. This document describes the functional design of the process to generate the ABC Classification for the Items and then update the same at Item level. ## Overview and Scope

Overview
Business Purpose
The Purpose of this integration is to assign Classification to Items based on which they will be cyclically counted and adjusted to maintain Inventory Accuracy. Scope
Scope is limited to copying Classification to Item Master. Scope does not include the Logic for generating Item classification. Return to Vendor process is not in scope of this document,
Functional Overview
- The frequency with which Items are counted your items depends upon the criticality of the item. Oracle Inventory fusion provides a feature to execute ABC Analysis based on the Onhand Stock of Items. The ABC analysis divides an inventory into different categories- "A items", "B items", "C items" , "D items" Varying in from very tightly control and accurate records to less tightly controlled and minimal records. Once the analysis is Run, an ABC Assignment Group is created with Details of Items in each Group. - A new Process will be created which will lookup the Items in the assignment group and updated the corresponding class in the Item Master EFF. # Business Objectives

The Objective is to enable ABC Classification Information generated in Fusion to be made available in WMS for Cycle Counting to be executed.

# Introduction

## Purpose

This Design Specification documents the detailed design updating ABC Classification on a given Item. This document describes the functional design of the process to generate the ABC Classification for the Items and then update the same at Item level. ## Overview and Scope

Overview
Business Purpose
The Purpose of this integration is to assign Classification to Items based on which they will be cyclically counted and adjusted to maintain Inventory Accuracy. Scope
Scope is limited to copying Classification to Item Master. Scope does not include the Logic for generating Item classification. Return to Vendor process is not in scope of this document,
Functional Overview
- The frequency with which Items are counted your items depends upon the criticality of the item. Oracle Inventory fusion provides a feature to execute ABC Analysis based on the Onhand Stock of Items. The ABC analysis divides an inventory into different categories- "A items", "B items", "C items" , "D items" Varying in from very tightly control and accurate records to less tightly controlled and minimal records. Once the analysis is Run, an ABC Assignment Group is created with Details of Items in each Group. - A new Process will be created which will lookup the Items in the assignment group and updated the corresponding class in the Item Master EFF. # Business Objectives

The Objective is to enable ABC Classification Information generated in Fusion to be made available in WMS for Cycle Counting to be executed.

| CR094 | [Anonymized Customer] | [Anonymized Customer] |

## Process Overview

- Setup ABC Assignment Group and assign Items to the classes. o Define ABC Classes
o Define an ABC Classification Set
o Define ABC Assignment Groups
o Perform an ABC Assignment
o View and Update ABC Item Assignments
- Pick all the Items in the ABC Assignment group. For each Item in the assignment group update the Item EFF Attribute “ABC Class” under the section “Attributes for WMS Integration” Under “[Anonymized Customer] Common Attributes” in the inventory org corresponding to that in the Assignment Group. # Mapping

# Introduction

## Purpose

This Design Specification documents the detailed design for items Cost Interface from Fusion to Oracle Cloud WMS. This document describes the functional design of the list of attributes which need to be interfaced from Fusion to Cloud WMS through Oracle Integrated Cloud Service (OIC) to update Item Cost (Cost Element – Material) in WMS. The design document also covers the event attribute mappings from Fusion to Oracle Cloud WMS Functional Columns. ## Overview and Scope

Overview
For performing Cycle Count transactions in WMS, item cost data is required. Since item cost is required in WMS for the Cycle Count approvals, synchronization service will be needed to send the create / update Cost information to Cloud WMS. Business Purpose
Cycle Counting will be done in Oracle Cloud WMS. For the Cycle Count approvals, the Item Standard Cost is required to trigger the approvals based on the Tolerance percentages set at Cycle Count level. Hence, a specific interface needs to be built between Fusion and Cloud WMS as per the Business Requirement to keep item cost data in sync between the two systems. This design document focuses on building an interface between Fusion and Cloud WMS so that item cost data can be kept in sync. Scope
The scope of this document is limited to functional design of the interface to communicate items’ standard cost additions and updates from Fusion to Cloud WMS System. Functional Overview
Fusion Cost Management is a source for all item cost information.

As such, it is a master repository to hold all cost data, which is defined at Item number and inventory organization level. Product Cost information is published to consuming systems with their related entities for downstream consumption, as per configured publication criteria, to determine what data elements (Item Attributes) get published to what systems and at what cadence. Fusion Cost Management will publish only the items and its cost that meet the publication criteria in the Cost Management for the WMS downstream system. Standard Cost of all the items that need to be cycle counted in the warehouses needs to be interfaced into the Item master in WMS. Standard Cost is maintained under different Cost Scenarios in Cost Accounting Work Area under Inventory Management. Only the Published Cost Scenarios’ data (Unit Cost of Cost Element - Material) of the Cost Organizations of [Anonymized Customer] (now) and UK (in future) needs to be pushed from Fusion to WMS. There can be 2 approaches for the Integration:
- The Integration can be event-based with point-to-point integration. While user runs the Update Standard Cost program for the selected Cost Scenario, system can push all the Items in the Cost Scenario along with its Cost details from Fusion to WMS
- The Integration can be batch-based program, which runs every 1 hour and will send the Cost data in Published status in the last 1 hour (from the previous run) from Fusion to WMS
The Cost Master should include the following details at minimum:
- Item Number
- Valuation Unit
- Status (Published)
- Effective Start Date
- Unit Cost (Cost Element – Material)
By integrating Fusion Item Cost Master to WMS, all the item’s Material cost details, as listed above, are expected to be integrated into WMS, which will help in processing the Cycle Count approvals accurately. With reference to storing the Cost in WMS, it has to be stored against the Item and Company combination. There needs to be a mapping between the Valuation Unit (Fusion) and Company code (WMS) maintained in order to store the Item Cost at Company level. # Business Objectives

The Cost Management (Cost Master) maintains master cost information enabling an enterprise to link all its critical cost data to one source, providing a common point of reference.

As part of the business process, costs need to be published from Cost Management to the Warehouse Management System (WMS). The integration solution is designed to enable scalable integrations to accommodate future requirements. The following objectives were captured during the Focus Stage and are addressed by the functional designs described in this document:

# Introduction

## Purpose

This Design Specification documents the detailed design for items Cost Interface from Fusion to Oracle Cloud WMS. This document describes the functional design of the list of attributes which need to be interfaced from Fusion to Cloud WMS through Oracle Integrated Cloud Service (OIC) to update Item Cost (Cost Element – Material) in WMS. The design document also covers the event attribute mappings from Fusion to Oracle Cloud WMS Functional Columns. ## Overview and Scope

**Overview**
For performing Cycle Count transactions in WMS, item cost data is required. Since item cost is required in WMS for the Cycle Count approvals, synchronization service will be needed to send the create / update Cost information to Cloud WMS. **Business Purpose**
Cycle Counting will be done in Oracle Cloud WMS. For the Cycle Count approvals, the Item Standard Cost is required to trigger the approvals based on the Tolerance percentages set at Cycle Count level. Hence, a specific interface needs to be built between Fusion and Cloud WMS as per the Business Requirement to keep item cost data in sync between the two systems. This design document focuses on building an interface between Fusion and Cloud WMS so that item cost data can be kept in sync. **Scope**
The scope of this document is limited to functional design of the interface to communicate items’ standard cost additions and updates from Fusion to Cloud WMS System.

**Functional Overview**
Fusion Cost Management is a source for all item cost information. As such, it is a master repository to hold all cost data, which is defined at Item number and inventory organization level. Product Cost information is published to consuming systems with their related entities for downstream consumption, as per configured publication criteria, to determine what data elements (Item Attributes) get published to what systems and at what cadence. Fusion Cost Management will publish only the items and its cost that meet the publication criteria in the Cost Management for the WMS downstream system. Standard Cost of all the items that need to be cycle counted in the warehouses needs to be interfaced into the Item master in WMS. Standard Cost is maintained under different Cost Scenarios in Cost Accounting Work Area under Inventory Management. Only the Published Cost Scenarios’ data (Unit Cost of Cost Element - Material) of the Cost Organizations of [Anonymized Customer] (now) and UK (in future) needs to be pushed from Fusion to WMS. There can be 2 approaches for the Integration:
- The Integration can be event-based with point-to-point integration. While user runs the Update Standard Cost program for the selected Cost Scenario, system can push all the Items in the Cost Scenario along with its Cost details from Fusion to WMS
- The Integration can be batch-based program, which runs every 1 hour and will send the Cost data in Published status in the last 1 hour (from the previous run) from Fusion to WMS
The Cost Master should include the following details at minimum:
- Item Number
- Valuation Unit
- Status (Published)
- Effective Start Date
- Unit Cost (Cost Element – Material)
By integrating Fusion Item Cost Master to WMS, all the item’s Material cost details, as listed above, are expected to be integrated into WMS, which will help in processing the Cycle Count approvals accurately. With reference to storing the Cost in WMS, it has to be stored against the Item and Company combination. There needs to be a mapping between the Valuation Unit (Fusion) and Company code (WMS) maintained in order to store the Item Cost at Company level. # Business Objectives

The Cost Management (Cost Master) maintains master cost information enabling an enterprise to link all its critical cost data to one source, providing a common point of reference.

As part of the business process, costs need to be published from Cost Management to the Warehouse Management System (WMS). The integration solution is designed to enable scalable integrations to accommodate future requirements. The following objectives were captured during the Focus Stage and are addressed by the functional designs described in this document:

This document specifies the business context, requirements, dependencies, and technical considerations for the technical team for the development & configuration for CR055- Create automatic Document Structure Templates for item classes. ## Overview

[Anonymized Customer] will maintain Its Key documentation by using Document objects in PLM. Document structure will be created under a parent document folder. The folder takes its unique identifier name from the part / item it relates to - Typically Doc-012345. This parent folder is in turn then related to the item. However, it relies on individuals setting up folder structures for each new item manually - Users will need to be carefully trained, to ensure Standardised folder structure and naming conventions. From this standardisation and harmonisation comes governance benefits - from ease of searching, expiry dates for folders and or documents, efficiency in one document to many parts scenarios like electronic component data and compliance sheets, etc. etc.

# Business Objectives

## Process Overview

Create a template based on item class to auto populate a consistent file folder structure for each new item. This template would create the structure and name each folder of document object. This would save considerable time for users / engineers, it would give a clean, repeatable doc structure leading to a global standard. (A key aspiration of the Novus project) And eliminate naming convention / part number issues. ## Business Requirements

Create automatic Document Structure Templates for specific item classes. Several document structures would exist for common item classes that require specification, quality and compliance data / evidence. Structure example:
As standard, templates do not exist for document objects. An extension would be required as follows:
Once an Item is created (in this example Item created = EPT-206371) a business event would fire to initiate the Integration Orchestration in OIC. The Integration process flow:
- End User will create new items in Product Development and save, eg. ETP-206371. Business Event:
- Item Create Event. Signals an Item is created. - OIC orchestration:
- Check if the Item Leaf ICC is applicable for document items to be created – See Mapping Table – eg. if Item is created against any of the Leaf Level ICC’s in the mapping table, e.g. ‘Software Internal’ proceed to create the document parent and item structure for every item in the Item Structure. - Create the Document parent Item. The Document Parent item will be created as follows:
- Parent Item Number is derived - prefixed with 'DST' and Full Item Number. The concatenation would be DST||<Item Number>, E.g. DST-EPT-206371
- Other mandatory values to create item are constant. - Create the document child object items under the document parent item based on:
- Pre-defined mapping – See Mapping Table
- The mapping table will contain the document items and names for each applicable ICC, e.g. For Software Internal, 4 child document objects – Release Notes, Instructions, Compliance, Binary Data
- The Document Child items will be created as follows using above example:
- Item Number is derived. Prefixed with ‘DST’ and including the Item Number and Document Object Name (predefined in mapping table).

The concatenation would be DST||‘-‘||<Item Number>||‘-‘||<Document Object> which as per our example would be created as DST-EPT-206371-Release Notes. - Item Class Name is derived. As per mapping table
- Item Description is derived based on the Document Object Name
- Other mandatory values to create item are constant. - Create the Document Parent Item as a related item to the Item Number, e.g., EPT-206371, using Item Relationships in Product Information Management (PIM). # Introduction

## Purpose

The objective of this document is to provide a Technical Specification to:
Establish a functional design to address key business objectives. Provide traceability between business requirements and the delivered components. Identify the touchpoints for any functional level integration. Capture any key dependencies. Provide high level functional design for [Anonymized Customer] ERP Leads and Technical Leads to confirm what will be delivered. Provide the necessary information with enough detail so that the technical teams, and/or external 3rd parties, have a clear understanding of the functional requirements that will enable them to design and build the extension component to satisfy the requirements. Assist the testing teams in understanding what to test. ## Scope

This document specifies the business context, requirements, dependencies, and technical considerations for the technical team for the development & configuration for CR055- Create automatic Document Structure Templates for item classes. ## Overview

[Anonymized Customer] will maintain Its Key documentation by using Document objects in PLM. Document structure will be created under a parent document folder. The folder takes its unique identifier name from the part / item it relates to - Typically Doc-012345. This parent folder is in turn then related to the item. However, it relies on individuals setting up folder structures for each new item manually - Users will need to be carefully trained, to ensure Standardised folder structure and naming conventions. From this standardisation and harmonisation comes governance benefits - from ease of searching, expiry dates for folders and or documents, efficiency in one document to many parts scenarios like electronic component data and compliance sheets, etc. etc.

# Business Objectives

## Process Overview

Create a template based on item class to auto populate a consistent file folder structure for each new item. This template would create the structure and name each folder of document object. This would save considerable time for users / engineers, it would give a clean, repeatable doc structure leading to a global standard. (A key aspiration of the Novus project) And eliminate naming convention / part number issues. ## Business Requirements

Create automatic Document Structure Templates for specific item classes. Several document structures would exist for common item classes that require specification, quality and compliance data / evidence. Structure example:
As standard, templates do not exist for document objects. An extension would be required as follows:
Once an Item is created (in this example Item created = EPT-206371) a business event would fire to initiate the Integration Orchestration in OIC. The Integration process flow:
- End User will create new items in Product Development and save, eg. ETP-206371. Business Event:
- Item Create Event. Signals an Item is created. - OIC orchestration:
- Check if the Item Leaf ICC is applicable for document items to be created – See Mapping Table – eg. if Item is created against any of the Leaf Level ICC’s in the mapping table, e.g. ‘Software Internal’ proceed to create the document parent and item structure for every item in the Item Structure. - Create the Document parent Item. The Document Parent item will be created as follows:
- Parent Item Number is derived - prefixed with 'DST' and Full Item Number. The concatenation would be DST||<Item Number>, E.g. DST-EPT-206371
- Other mandatory values to create item are constant. - Create the document child object items under the document parent item based on:
- Pre-defined mapping – See Mapping Table
- The mapping table will contain the document items and names for each applicable ICC, e.g. For Software Internal, 4 child document objects – Release Notes, Instructions, Compliance, Binary Data
- The Document Child items will be created as follows using above example:
- Item Number is derived. Prefixed with ‘DST’ and including the Item Number and Document Object Name (predefined in mapping table).

The concatenation would be DST||‘-‘||<Item Number>||‘-‘||<Document Object> which as per our example would be created as DST-EPT-206371-Release Notes. - Item Class Name is derived. As per mapping table
- Item Description is derived based on the Document Object Name
- Other mandatory values to create item are constant. - Create the Document Parent Item as a related item to the Item Number, e.g., EPT-206371, using Item Relationships in Product Information Management (PIM). (Via the UI, this is on the Manage Item Relationships page). - Item Relationship will be created with the predefined Relationship Type ‘Collateral’. # Risk Matrix

# Introduction

## Purpose

The objective of this document is to provide a Functional Specification to:
Establish a functional design to address key business objectives required for Item integration to GTM to maintain Trade compliance. Identify the touchpoints for the functional level integration. Provide high level functional process design for [Anonymized Customer] ERP Leads and Technical Leads. Capturing data mapping between two systems in the context of this integration. Provide the necessary information with enough detail so that the technical teams, and/or external 3rd parties, have a clear understanding of the functional requirements that will enable them to design and build the integration component to satisfy the requirements. ## Scope

This document specifies the business context, functional requirements, and details to Integrate the Item Data to GTM once it is created or Updated in Fusion PDH. Item gets created or Updated in Fusion PDH System. Once the Item is created or update in PDH, it needs to be integrated to GTM with the Item Attributes. The Item and Item Attributes are used in GTM for Product classification which is required for Trade Transactions. ## Functional Overview

[Anonymized Customer] manages core item definitions within the [Anonymized Customer] Fusion Product Lifecycle Management Cloud (PLM) suite. [Anonymized Customer] PLM will serve as the item master (‘single source of truth’) for downstream logistics systems: [Anonymized Customer] Global Trade Management Cloud (GTM) and [Anonymized Customer] Warehouse Management Cloud (WMS).

The business need for this integration is to provide the required item data from the [Anonymized Customer] Fusion Cloud source system (from which [Anonymized Customer] PLM is part of) to external target system GTM to support trade compliance screening operations and business processes within those modules. For the purposes of this integration, only PDH module is required from the PLM suite since it contains all the necessary item master data there. # Business Objectives

## Process Overview

Trade Compliance screening requires item data elements and its attributes. PDH supports creating an item of structures standard, model, and option class. Flow of item from PDH to GTM will be as follows:
In GTM, item will be created as ITEM object with trade details capturing the product classification code, Item origin. In PDH the product classification is maintained at master org level which is copied into all the inventory org the item is associated with and country of origin is maintained at inventory org level. # Mapping

# Pre-Conditions

- Items should be defined in PDH Item master organization. - Item should be shippable, sellable, and receivable. - COO should be added to the respective inventory Organization.

### Assumptions

- Mapping between Inventory Organizations in SCM Cloud and GTM Facilities needs to be setup for this integration to extract data. - In case, if no records are extracted during the current schedule period. The integration will end normal. - In case of any success/error in the integration, a notification email will be sent to the mail list configured in the OIC lookup. - Product Classification Codes and Country of Origin populated against the item in Fusion has to be in sync with GTM to interface the data successfully from Fusion to GTM without fail. ### High Level Approach

- Assemble to Order (ATO) Option Class, Pick to Order (PTO) Option Class, Pick to Order (PTO) will be excluded as part of Fusion Item Extraction Report. - Non-Inventory Items (Software Items) having item class DOM_SOFTWARE_EXTERNAL_ICC, DOM_SOFTWARE_INTERNAL_ICC will only be sent to GTM. - Items having Country of Origin populated against Inventory Org in Fusion will interface to GTM.

- Items having product Classification Codes populated will interface to GTM. - Item Class against each item will interface from Fusion to GTM. - Primary Unit of Measure against each item will interface from Fusion to GTM. - Only Fluids Items will have Precursor checkbox (Y/N) enabled. - The Item Master Bulk Export “XxPublishItemMasterErpToGtm” integration will be a scheduled integration which will trigger the custom ESS job “Xx_INT009_ITEM_MASTER_EXTRACT_ESS_JOB”. - Item Master details along with Product Classification Codes are extracted from SCM Cloud (SaaS) using the BI Publisher tool. - The extracted Item Master records data file is placed in UCM. - The records from the file will be inserted into custom ATP table - “XXDOM_GTM_ITEM_DETAILS_T” & those records will be divided into batch of 200 records in ATP through Item PLSQL procedure. - The Item information will be interfaced into batches to GTM cloud using GTM Publish “ItemMaster” business object service. - GTM will send the transmission report to OIC which consists of status of each record - Success/Fail. In case of fail records, the notification email will be sent to concern users with error records file. ### Pre-Requisites

# Introduction

## Purpose

The objective of this document is to provide a Functional Specification to:
Establish a functional design to address key business objectives required for Order Management to GTM integration for Trade Compliance Screening. Identify the touchpoints for the functional level integration. Provide high level functional process design for [Anonymized Customer] ERP Leads and Technical Leads
Capturing data mapping between two systems in the context of this integration
Provide the necessary information with enough detail so that the technical teams, and/or external 3rd parties, have a clear understanding of the functional requirements that will enable them to design and build the integration component to satisfy the requirements. ## Scope

This document specifies the business context, functional requirements, and details to integrate Order Management with Global Trade Management (GTM) for trade Compliance screening. As per current design Sales orders for [Anonymized Customer] should go for Restricted party Screening, Sanctions Screening and Trade Agreement qualification. ## Functional Overview

We can use Order Management with trade management solution to create and manage trade transactions that comply with global import trade rules, export global trade rules, and other trade regulations that a country or region requires. In Oracle Fusion Order Management, Trade Compliance Screening can be done in either way
- At the time of order submission
- As part of orchestration step. This has more control as we can have the trade screening done at any step of the orchestration e.g., after scheduling, after reservation etc. This is the recommended way for [Anonymized Customer] as sales order lines are to be send to GTM only after scheduling.

Once Sales order is submitted, the trade compliance should get triggered for each fulfilment line after the Global Order Promising has scheduled the order. The order fulfilment line should not get progressed to next step until or unless trade screening is successfully completed and is passed. In case the order has multiple lines and at least one line has failed trade agreement screening, all other lines should also not progress to the next step even if they have passed the trade agreement screening. Sales Order information going to GTM should have following information:
- RPLS
- SHIP_FROM
- SHIP_TO
- SOLD_TO
- Sanctions
- Destination Country (SHIP_TO)
Following should be the steps that needs to be followed. - Submit the Sales Order
- Fulfilment Line gets Scheduled. - Request Screening for Trade Compliance (Integration from OM to GTM)
- Wait for Trade Compliance Screening (Integration from GTM to OM)
- Proceed with the next steps of fulfilment once all lines passed screening. In case of changes to the configured item, the existing line in fusion would be cancelled and new line would be added to the same sales order. This line will be treated as new trade transaction in GTM. For each Sales Order Line, there will be 1 trade transaction with multiple lines (if applicable based on structure). # Business Objectives

## Process Overview

Assumptions:
- Configured items for drop ship scenario ([Anonymized Customer] UK / DLG configured as Supplier in fusion) will not be screened for components in GTM. - For Configured items Drop ship orders placed in Benelux channel, PO will not be screened in GTM. - For spare orders placed in Benelux channel for 3rd party supplier, PO will not be screened in GTM as SO will be screened as part of Drop Ship orders. - Transfer orders in Benelux will not be screened in GTM. - RMA needs screening in GTM for sanctioned countries. Receipt Only and Return for credit and return the item line type will only be sent to GTM. Return for credit line type will not be sent to GTM. - Stock Loan Order (Getting items for from [Anonymized Customer] sites into Benelux channel) will not need GTM screening. - Hire Order (Shipment to customer) will require GTM screening for SO & Shipment. - Hire conversion SO and shipment will not require GTM screening as it is virtual.

- Ad hoc part orders (Orders from Benelux inv org to Customer) will be screened for SO, Shipment & RMA (parts returned from customer) in GTM. - Depot repair orders/ Inhouse Repair order (Eg: get the printer from customer site and repair and send back) will be screened for SO, Shipment & RMA in GTM. - Monthly warranty claims (Defective part returned from sales channel to Manufacturing Org) will not go through GTM screening. - Truck inventory replenishment will require PO screening if PO is created with 3rd party supplier. If there is TO create no screening in GTM required. - Deposit Invoice Orders will be screened for shippable lines only in GTM. - No line or order cancellation will be initiated from GTM. - Software items will be screened in GTM. - Cancellation / Scheduling of line in fusion will trigger to OIC. For this OIC will filter for not sending to GTM and updating fusion with response so that orchestration can move to next step. Functional Configuration

Once trade transaction screening is completed, the status of the trade transaction will be changed in GTM and the response of the trade transaction will be sent to the fusion. ## Functional Overview

We can use Order Management with trade management solution to create and manage trade transactions that comply with global import trade rules, export global trade rules, and other trade regulations that a country or region requires. In Oracle Fusion Order Management, Trade Compliance Screening can be done in either way
- At the time of order submission
- As part of orchestration step. This has more control as we can have the trade screening done at any step of the orchestration e.g., after scheduling, after reservation etc.

This is the recommended way for [Anonymized Customer] as sales order lines are to be send to GTM only after scheduling. Once Sales order is submitted, the trade compliance should get triggered for each fulfilment line after the Global Order Promising has scheduled the order. The order fulfilment line should not get progressed to next step until or unless trade screening is successfully completed and is passed. In case the order has multiple lines and at least one line has failed trade agreement screening, all other lines should also not progress to the next step even if they have passed the trade agreement screening. ### Assumptions

### High Level Approach

- Sales Order Trade Compliance Response will be sent from GTM to Fusion ERP system. - GTM sends a response automatically after the Trade Compliance screening process in GTM is completed incase of success scenario. An event is generated and “XxSoComplianceResponseGtmToErp ” integration is triggered.

Incase of error scenario(negative testing), GTM Trade Compliance manually sends the error response
- OIC process populates the ATP DB table with the status information from GTM
- OIC process checks if all the lines have been processed and if true then all the lines have the TC passed and OM is updated with “Trade Compliance Screening Passed “status else if any one line fails the OM is updated with “Trade Compliance Under Review “ for individual lines and incase of lines belonging to a Shipset, all the lines in the shipset are updated as “Trade Compliance Under Review “. All other lines within the Sales Order which have passed the “Trade Compliance Screening” proceed further to the next step in the process
- In case of error, Common Error Handler is invoked to handle the error and an error notification is sent to the stakeholders

### High Level Approach

- Sales Order Trade Compliance Response will be sent from GTM to Fusion ERP system. - GTM sends a response automatically after the Trade Compliance screening process in GTM is completed incase of success scenario. An event is generated and “XxSoComplianceResponseGtmToErp ” integration is triggered.

Incase of error scenario(negative testing), GTM Trade Compliance manually sends the error response
- OIC process populates the ATP DB table with the status information from GTM
- OIC process checks if all the lines have been processed and if true , then all the lines that have the overall status as TC passed are updated as “Trade Compliance Screening Passed “ in the Fusion OM application else if any one line fails, the OM application is updated with “Trade Compliance Under Review “ for individual lines and incase of lines belonging to a Shipset, all the lines in the shipset are updated as “Trade Compliance Under Review “ and individual lines within the shipset are updated with the actual TC statuses. All other lines within the Sales Order which have passed the “Trade Compliance Screening” are marked as “Trade Compliance Screening Passed “and will proceed further to the next step in the process
- There can be a scenario where in the user has corrected one of the failed TC status or all applicable TC statuses as “Passed” and sent to OIC. In this case, the Reprocess flag is updated so that the new integration (XXSOComplianceResponseResubmitGTMToERP) is invoked which would process the corrected lines and sends the updated TC status as passed to Fusion OM application. - In case of error, Common Error Handler is invoked to handle the error and an error notification is sent to the stakeholders

[Anonymized Customer] gets created or Updated in Fusion. Once the [Anonymized Customer] is created or update in Fusion, it needs to be integrated to GTM. This document specifies the business context, functional requirements, and details to Integrate the [Anonymized Customer] details to GTM in order to Perform Trade compliance screening of the [Anonymized Customer] once it is created or Updated in Fusion

## Functional Overview

Screening is a process whereby each individual or company (business partners) with whom you are planning to do business is screened against the restricted party list (denied, debarred and/or restricted parties) to check whether you can conduct business with them. GTM provides the functionality to download Restricted Parties list from third party content providers and perform screening of involved parties against the list of ‘Restricted’ parties identified by the government.

When you first download restricted parties into GTM from a content provider, you can compare all your parties in GTM to the entire restricted party list. As a content provider updates the restricted party lists, based on updates to the regulations, content providers will only send in the updates to the existing lists in GTM, also known as a delta list. At this time, GTM will then perform delta screening where all parties in GTM are screened against the delta list. # Business Objectives

## Process Overview

[Anonymized Customer] deals with multiple customers in its selling process. Every valid customer (internal and external) will be defined in Oracle Fusion, and this will be considered as source of truth. The typical customer data model is as shown below. The customer master data will be shared with multiple downstream applications to enable their processes related to selling. Trade compliance screening related to sales order fulfilment will be managed in GTM application. Fulfilment order lines will be created in Oracle SCM Cloud and interfaced to GTM for screening for trade compliance. To facilitate restricted party screening (RPLS ) and to screen for restricted countries (Sanctions), GTM needs customer master data from fusion. This integration is aimed to source all the customer master data required by GTM. The primary customer data required are party aka customer, customer account number, customer site addresses, and their contacts. Customer master data will be published to GTM in batch mode through OIC. Any addition/modification to customer data relevant to logistics, will result triggering integration message. This integration will deliver a party glog XML payload to GTM. The following mapping will be considered while creating party in GTM:
CUS – Party Number – Party Site Number
Each party will be associated to location. Company name in party will be party name and location name will be party site name. Location will have the party site address mapped to it. For Eg: CUS-5476-5124
To map the SOLD TO party for screening party from fusion is also sent. It is mapped as:
CUS - Party Number
This party will have location associated with party address to it. For Eg: CUS-5476
All the integrated customers will be created in GTM as parties.

This integration is aimed to source all the supplier master data required for trade compliance screening. The primary supplier data required are supplier, site addresses, and their contacts. Supplier master data will be published to GTM in batch mode through OIC. Any addition/modification to supplier data relevant to trade compliance, will result triggering integration message. This integration will deliver a party glog XML payload to GTM. The following mapping will be considered while creating party in GTM:
SUP - Vendor Number – Vendor Site Id
Party First Name will be Supplier Name and each party will be associated with location which the supplier site id. Location Name will be supplier site name. Location will have the supplier site address mapped to it. For e.g. : SUP-55489-300000012426263
All the integrated Suppliers will be created in GTM as parties. # Mapping

# Introduction

## Purpose

The objective of this document is to provide a Functional Specification to:
Establish a functional design to address key business objectives required for Procurement to GTM integration for Trade Compliance Screening. Identify the touchpoints for the functional level integration. Provide high level functional process design for [Anonymized Customer] ERP Leads and Technical Leads
Capturing data mapping between two systems in the context of this integration
Provide the necessary information with enough detail so that the technical teams, and/or external 3rd parties, have a clear understanding of the functional requirements that will enable them to design and build the integration component to satisfy the requirements. ## Scope

This document specifies the business context, functional requirements, and details to integrate Purchase order with Global Trade Management (GTM) for trade Compliance screening. As per current design Purchase orders for [Anonymized Customer] should go for Restricted party Screening, Sanctions Screening. ## Functional Overview

Fusion Procurement can be integrated with Global trade management to create and manage Purchase order trade transactions that comply with global import trade rules, export global trade rules, and other trade regulations that a country or region requires. Purchase orders will be integrated to GTM for compliance screening once the PO is approved in fusion Procurement. The Purchase orders created in Fusion gets integrated into the GTM as a trade transaction. The status of the PO will be open before the PO transmission to GTM. The Trade transaction  is screened for compliance check in GTM and the response of the trade transaction will be sent to the fusion.

Purchase Order information going to GTM should have following information:
- RPLS
- SHIP_FROM
- SHIP_TO
- SUPPLIER
- Sanctions
- Source Country (SHIP_FROM)

# Business Objectives

## Process Overview

Purchase Orders created in Fusion Procurement will be integrated to the GTM for compliance screening (RPLS/Sanctions). Once PO is approved it gets integrated to GTM as a Trade Transaction. Once trade transaction screening is completed, the status of the trade transaction will be changed in GTM and the responses of the trade transaction will be sent to the fusion. •	If screening is passed in GTM then PO status is OPEN
•	If screening is failed/Requires Review in GTM then PO status is ON HOLD
For each Purchase order(single line/Multi Line), there will be 1 trade transaction. Drop ship PO’ and Stock order Back to Back PO wont flow to GTM since the compliance screening is done at SO level. Functional Configuration
RPLS screening process:
- For each PO, we have trade transaction created
- SHIP_FROM, SUPPLIER involved party in trade transaction line will be matched with restricted parties list provided by Descartes. - Status will be updated to TS_RPLS_PASSED / TS_RPLS_REQUIRES_REVIEW /TS_ RPLS_FAILED. - TS_RPLS_REQUIRES_REVIEW status transaction will be manually reviewed by the trade compliance team to set it to TS_RPLS_PASSED / TS_RPLS_FAILED. Sanction screening process:
- For each PO, we have trade transaction created
- Sanction screening will be done Import Orders. - Sanction screening is done for following conditions:
- Sanction List for Europe
- Sanction List for UK
- Sanction list for US
- Sanction for Iron & Steel items for Europe
For a,b,c : Transaction line Source country of SHIP_FROM involved party is screened against sanctioned country list configured in GTM. For d: Transaction line containing iron & steel item / components entering Europe (SHIP_FROM outside Europe, SHIP_TO within Europe) will be sanctioned. This will require manually review by the Trade compliance team to resolve. - TS_SANCTION_COUNTRIES_PASSED/ TS_SANCTION_COUNTRIES_FAILED will be status according to the screening result for the transaction line.

The response is sent automatically for all the status types of PO in GTM

Provide the necessary information with enough detail so that the technical teams, and/or external 3rd parties, have a clear understanding of the functional requirements that will enable them to design and build the integration component to satisfy the requirements. ## Scope

The Scope of the Outbound integration from GTM to Fusion Procurement is to Update the Purchase order screening status to Fusion. On the basis of Screening status PO will be Put on hold or remain in Open status. ## Functional Overview

Purchase orders will be integrated to GTM for compliance screening once the PO is approved in fusion Procurement. The Purchase orders created in Fusion gets integrated into the GTM as a trade transaction. The status of the PO will be open before the PO transmission to GTM. The Trade transaction is screened for compliance check in GTM and the response of the trade transaction will be sent to the fusion. If screening is passed in GTM then PO status is OPEN. If screening is failed/Requires Review in GTM then PO status is ON HOLD. # Business Objectives

## Process Overview

Purchase Orders created in Fusion Procurement will be integrated to the GTM for compliance screening (RPLS/Sanctions).

Once PO is approved it gets integrated to GTM as a Trade Transaction. Once trade transaction screening is completed, the status of the trade transaction will be changed in GTM and the responses of the trade transaction will be sent to the fusion. Functional Configuration
RPLS screening process:
- For each PO, we have trade transaction created. - SHIP_FROM, SUPPLIER involved party in trade transaction line will be matched with restricted parties list provided by Descartes. - Status will be updated to TS_RPLS_PASSED / TS_RPLS_REQUIRES_REVIEW /TS_ RPLS_FAILED. - TS_RPLS_REQUIRES_REVIEW status transaction will be manually reviewed by the trade compliance team to set it to TS_RPLS_PASSED / TS_RPLS_FAILED. Sanction screening process:
- For each PO, we have trade transaction created. - Sanction screening will be done Import Orders. - Sanction screening is done for following conditions:
- Sanction List for Europe
- Sanction List for UK
- Sanction list for US
- Sanction for Iron & Steel items for Europe
For a,b,c : Transaction line Source country of SHIP_FROM involved party is screened against sanctioned country list configured in GTM. For d: Transaction line containing iron & steel item / components entering Europe (SHIP_FROM outside Europe, SHIP_TO within Europe) will be sanctioned. This will require manually review by the Trade compliance team to resolve. - TS_SANCTION_COUNTRIES_PASSED/ TS_SANCTION_COUNTRIES_FAILED will be status according to the screening result for the transaction line. The response is sent automatically for all the status types of PO in GTM

This document specifies the business context, functional requirements, and details to Integrate Product classification codes updated for the Item to Fusion PDH once Updated in GTM. ## Functional Overview

[Anonymized Customer] manages core item definitions within the Oracle Fusion Product Lifecycle Management Cloud (PLM) suite. Oracle PLM will serve as the item master (‘single source of truth’) for downstream logistics systems: Oracle Global Trade Management Cloud (GTM) and Oracle Warehouse Management Cloud (WMS). For the purposes of this integration, only PDH module is required from the PLM suite since it contains all the necessary product classification attributes. Every company has the responsibility to classify all goods and raw materials if they are the importer or exporter of record in any given country. This ensures that they comply with different export and import control regimes and also that the proper duty is being paid.

Once the product classification codes are updated in GTM, the information is passed to PDH and it gets updated in item attributes. # Business Objectives

## Process Overview

Trade Compliance screening requires item data elements and its attributes. PDH supports to maintain the product classification attributes which is required for cross border trade. Flow of Product classification codes from GTM to PDH will be as follows:
In GTM, item will be created as ITEM object with trade details capturing the product classification code, Item origin. This integration is for updates done on GTM for product classification code for items as trade compliance team will be more aware these data. Whenever a new item will be created in PDH it will flow to GTM. Trade compliance team will then update the classification code under trade details of item object in GTM. On saving the data response will be triggered back to PDH to update the corresponding columns in PDH for classification. # Mapping

# Introduction

## Purpose

The objective of this document is to provide a Functional Specification to:
Establish a functional design to address key business objectives required for Item BOM integration to GTM to maintain Trade compliance. Identify the touchpoints for the functional level integration. Provide high level functional process design for [Anonymized Customer] ERP Leads and Technical Leads. Capturing data mapping between two systems in the context of this integration. Provide the necessary information with enough detail so that the technical teams, and/or external 3rd parties, have a clear understanding of the functional requirements that will enable them to design and build the integration component to satisfy the requirements. ## Scope

This document specifies the business context, functional requirements, and details to Integrate the Item BOM Data to GTM once it is created or Updated in Fusion PDH. Item Structure gets created or Updated in Fusion PDH System. Once the Item structure is created or update in PDH, it needs to be integrated to GTM. The Item structure is used in GTM for Sanction check and Trade agreement Qualification. ## Functional Overview

[Anonymized Customer] is a leading global industrial printing brand that serves the commercial printing sector, providing digital inkjet printers and control systems for labelling and printing solutions. So for their finished good items that is manufactured they have bill of material. In PDH, a Bill of Materials is called a structure. When you add an item to a parent item, you create a simple structure. A structure holds all the items and documents that make up an assembly or subassembly.

For [Anonymized Customer] business has structures that are standard, model, option class. The standard structure and configured item structure needs to be sent to GTM for screening at components level for Country of Origin, restricted party screening and sanction (restricted countries). This integration is responsible for sending the standard structure and configured item structure to GTM. # Business Objectives

## Process Overview

The flow of item structure from PDH to GTM is as follows:
Item structure pertaining to master org and all the associated inventory org will be sent to GTM. In GTM, it is captured in Trade Item structure object. For each inventory org there will be trade item structure created. Each Trade item structure will have the first level of BOM. For second level of BOM will be stored as separate Trade item structure object. # Mapping

## Purpose

The objective of this document is to provide a Functional Specification to:
Establish a functional design to address key business objectives required for Shipment Screening from Fusion Inventory to GTM integration
Identify the touchpoints for the functional level integration. Provide high level functional process design for [Anonymized Customer] ERP Leads and Technical Leads
Capturing data mapping between two systems in the context of this integration
Provide the necessary information with enough detail so that the technical teams, and/or external 3rd parties, have a clear understanding of the functional requirements that will enable them to design and build the integration component to satisfy the requirements. ## Scope

This document specifies the business context, functional requirements, and details to integrate Fusion Inventory shipments with Global Trade Management (GTM) for trade Compliance screening. As per current design Shipments for [Anonymized Customer] should go for Restricted party Screening, Sanctions Screening and Product Classification Screening. ## Functional Overview

Pick Confirm shipment Lines created in Fusion Inventory will be integrated to the GTM for compliance screening. The Pick Confirm shipment Lines created in Fusion gets integrated to GTM as a Trade Transaction. Once trade transaction screening is completed, the status of the trade transaction will be changed in GTM and the responses of the trade transaction will be sent to the fusion. Shipment information going to GTM should have following information:
- RPLS
- SHIP_FROM
- SHIP_TO
- SOLD_TO
- Sanctions
- Destination Country (SHIP_TO)

# Business Objectives

## Process Overview

Once the Fusion OM Order status is Awaiting Shipping, the shipment creation is carried out in Fusion Inventory Management.

User creates a shipment and perform pick Release. For Items having No control, pick release and Pick confirm happens together and for Lot and serial control Pick confirm has to be done. Shipping parameter- pick confirm and Inventory Business Event configuration for GTM screening to be enabled in Inventory management. The Trade transaction created in GTM with the naming format SHIP-Pick slip no
•	If screening is passed in GTM then Pick Confirm Line can be released for Ship Confirm
•	If screening is failed in GTM then Pick Confirm Line cannot be Ship Confirmed
Shipping Parameter:
Inventory Business Event configuration
For each Shipment, there will be 1 trade transaction. RPLS screening process:
- For each Shipment, we have trade transaction created with line information. - SHIP_TO, SOLD_TO involved party in trade transaction line will be matched with restricted parties list provided by Descartes. - Status will be updated to TS_RPLS_PASSED / TS_RPLS_REQUIRES_REVIEW /TS_ RPLS_FAILED. - TS_RPLS_REQUIRES_REVIEW status transaction will be manually reviewed by the trade compliance team to set it to TS_RPLS_PASSED / TS_RPLS_FAILED. Sanction screening process:
- For each shipment, we have trade transaction created with line information. - Sanction screening will be done only for Export Orders. - Sanction screening is done for following conditions:
- Sanction List for Europe
- Sanction List for UK
- Sanction list for US Origin item / components
- Sanction for Iron & Steel items for Europe
- Sanction list for RMA
For a,b,e, : Transaction line Destination country of SHIP_TO involved party is screened against sanctioned country list configured in GTM. For c: Transaction line item / components Country of Origin = US along with SHIP_TO is screened. For d: Transaction line containing iron & steel item / components entering Europe (SHIP_FROM outside Europe, SHIP_TO within Europe) will be sanctioned. This will require manually review by the Trade compliance team to resolve. - TS_SANCTION_COUNTRIES_PASSED/ TS_SANCTION_COUNTRIES_FAILED will be status according to the screening result for the transaction line. Product classification Process
- Product classification look up would happen from item Master
- TS_Product_classification status would be updated to TS_Product_classification_complete or TS_Product_classification_incomplete or TS_Product_classification_not started
When trade transaction has RPLS, Sanction and Product classification has status TS_RPLS_PASSED & TS_SANCTION_COUNTRIES_PASSED  and TS_PRODUCT_CLASSIFICATION_COMPLETE response is sent automatically. In case of failure of trade transaction, the response is sent manually by Trade compliance team and the shipment has to be put on Hold.

### Assumptions

- Mapping between Inventory Organizations in SCM Cloud and GTM Facilities needs to be setup for this integration to extract data. - In case, if no records are extracted during the current schedule period. The integration will end normal. - In case of any success/error in the integration, a notification email will be sent to the mail list configured in the OIC lookup. - Item Master and Supplier needs to interface first in GTM before interfacing Trading Partner Items to GTM. - Trading Partner Item must be created first in GTM as part of Trading Partner Item data page as well to reside under Item in Item Master page in GTM. ### High Level Approach

- Only Trading Partner of Type “Supplier” has to be fetched as part of report from fusion. - Trading Partner Item created only in “Master Org” level will be fetched from fusion to interface to GTM.

- The Trading Partner Item Bulk Export “XxPublishTradingItemsErpToGtm” integration will be a scheduled integration which will trigger the custom ESS job “Xx_INT029_TRADING_ITEM_EXTRACT_ESS_JOB” in fusion. - Trading Partner Item details are extracted from SCM Cloud (SaaS) using the BI Publisher tool. - The extracted Trading Partner Item records data file is placed in UCM. - The records from the file will be inserted into custom ATP table - “XXDOM_GTM_TRADING_ITEM_DETAILS_T” & those records will be divided into batch of 200 records in ATP through Item PLSQL procedure. - The Trading Partner Item information will be interfaced into batches to GTM cloud using GTM Publish “PartnerItem” business object service. - Trading Partner Item to reside under Item as well will be interfaced to GTM using GTM Publish “ItemMaster” business object service. - GTM will send the transmission report to OIC which consists of status of each record - Success/Fail. In case of fail records, the notification email will be sent to concern users with error records file. ### Pre-Requisites

- Send Email Integration “XxCommonNotificationHandler” should be deployed in the OIC. - Lookup “XxDominoCommonLookup” should be present with all the required details regarding success/error email notify flag, success and error notify ToEmail Address in OIC. - Lookup “XxDominoConstantLookup” should be present with all the required details regarding success and error notify FromEmail Address in OIC. - GTM Constant field with their values should be deployed in the OIC Lookup “XxDominoGtmConstantLookup”. - GTM Transmission Report Response integration “XxGtmTransmissionResponseCallback” should be deployed in OIC. # Integration Analysis – XxPublishTradingItemsErpToGtm

Establish a functional design to address key business objectives. Provide traceability between business requirements and the delivered components. Assist the testing teams in understanding what to test. ## Scope

This document specifies the business context, requirements, dependencies, and technical considerations for the technical team for the development & configuration for CR077c- Fusion Exchange Rates to GTM Integration. ## Overview

Operating and continuing to actively maintain a Trade Compliance program is a vital component of doing business in the modern and constantly changing landscape of global trade. An effective program seeks to ensure adherence to all relevant trade regulations in all operating countries, and ultimately to protect and avoid companies being exposed to risk that can include delays, penalties, and even loss of trade privileges. Compliance programs should include clearly defined processes and procedures for screening customers and vendors, reviewing all shipments, ensuring compliance with applicable government sanctions, applying for licenses to export or import goods, checking business is not conducted with third parties in embargoed countries, and generally ensuring that all requirements (regulatory and also those driven by company policy) are met regarding exports and imports.
