# Introduction

## Purpose

The objective of this document is to provide a Functional Specification to:
Establish a functional design to address key business objectives required for Order Management to GTM integration for Trade Compliance Screening. Identify the touchpoints for the functional level integration. Provide high level functional process design for [Anonymized Customer] ERP Leads and Technical Leads
Capturing data mapping between two systems in the context of this integration
Provide the necessary information with enough detail so that the technical teams, and/or external 3rd parties, have a clear understanding of the functional requirements that will enable them to design and build the integration component to satisfy the requirements. ## Scope

This document specifies the business context, functional requirements, and details to integrate Order Management with Global Trade Management (GTM) for trade Compliance screening. As per current design Sales orders for [Anonymized Customer] should go for Restricted party Screening, Sanctions Screening and Trade Agreement qualification. ## Functional Overview

We can use Order Management with trade management solution to create and manage trade transactions that comply with global import trade rules, export global trade rules, and other trade regulations that a country or region requires. In Oracle Fusion Order Management, Trade Compliance Screening can be done in either way
- At the time of order submission
- As part of orchestration step. This has more control as we can have the trade screening done at any step of the orchestration e.g., after scheduling, after reservation etc. This is the recommended way for [Anonymized Customer] as sales order lines are to be send to GTM only after scheduling.

Once Sales order is submitted, the trade compliance should get triggered for each fulfilment line after the Global Order Promising has scheduled the order. The order fulfilment line should not get progressed to next step until or unless trade screening is successfully completed and is passed. In case the order has multiple lines and at least one line has failed trade agreement screening, all other lines should also not progress to the next step even if they have passed the trade agreement screening. Sales Order information going to GTM should have following information:
- RPLS
- SHIP_FROM
- SHIP_TO
- SOLD_TO
- Sanctions
- Destination Country (SHIP_TO)
Following should be the steps that needs to be followed. - Submit the Sales Order
- Fulfilment Line gets Scheduled. - Request Screening for Trade Compliance (Integration from OM to GTM)
- Wait for Trade Compliance Screening (Integration from GTM to OM)
- Proceed with the next steps of fulfilment once all lines passed screening. In case of changes to the configured item, the existing line in fusion would be cancelled and new line would be added to the same sales order. This line will be treated as new trade transaction in GTM. For each Sales Order Line, there will be 1 trade transaction with multiple lines (if applicable based on structure). # Business Objectives

# Introduction

## Purpose

The objective of this document is to provide a Functional Specification to:
Establish a functional design to address key business objectives required for Transfer Order Shipment Screening from Fusion Inventory to GTM integration
Identify the touchpoints for the functional level integration. Provide high level functional process design for [Anonymized Customer] ERP Leads and Technical Leads
Capturing data mapping between two systems in the context of this integration
Provide the necessary information with enough detail so that the technical teams, and/or external 3rd parties, have a clear understanding of the functional requirements that will enable them to design and build the integration component to satisfy the requirements. ## Scope

This document specifies the business context, functional requirements, and details to integrate Fusion Inventory shipments with Global Trade Management (GTM) for trade Compliance screening. As per current design Shipments for [Anonymized Customer] should go for Restricted party Screening, Sanctions Screening and Product Classification Screening. ## Functional Overview

Transfer Order Pick Confirm Shipment Lines created in Fusion Inventory will be integrated to the GTM for compliance screening. The Pick Confirm Shipment Lines created in Fusion gets integrated to GTM as a Trade Transaction. Once trade transaction screening is completed, the status of the trade transaction will be changed in GTM, and the responses of the trade transaction will be sent to the fusion. Shipment information going to GTM should have following information:
- RPLS
- SHIP_FROM
- SHIP_TO
- SOLD_TO
- Sanctions
- Destination Country (SHIP_TO)

# Business Objectives

## Process Overview

Once the Fusion OM Order status is Awaiting Shipping, the shipment creation is carried out in Fusion Inventory Management. User creates a shipment and perform pick Release.

For Items having No control, pick release and Pick confirm happens together and for Lot and serial control Pick confirm has to be done. Shipping parameter- pick confirm and Inventory Business Event configuration for GTM screening to be enabled in Inventory management. The Trade transaction created in GTM with the naming format SHIP-Pick slip no
• If screening is passed in GTM then Pick Confirm Line can be released for Ship Confirm
• If screening is failed in GTM then Pick Confirm Line cannot be Ship Confirmed
Shipping Parameter:
Inventory Business Event configuration
For each Shipment, there will be 1 trade transaction. RPLS screening process:
- For each Shipment, we have trade transaction created with line information. - SHIP_TO, SOLD_TO involved party in trade transaction line will be matched with restricted parties list provided by Descartes. - Status will be updated to TS_RPLS_PASSED / TS_RPLS_REQUIRES_REVIEW /TS_ RPLS_FAILED. - TS_RPLS_REQUIRES_REVIEW status transaction will be manually reviewed by the trade compliance team to set it to TS_RPLS_PASSED / TS_RPLS_FAILED. Sanction screening process:
- For each shipment, we have trade transaction created with line information. - Sanction screening will be done only for Export Orders. - Sanction screening is done for following conditions:
- Sanction List for Europe
- Sanction List for UK
- Sanction list for US Origin item / components
- Sanction for Iron & Steel items for Europe
- Sanction list for RMA
For a,b,e: Transaction line Destination country of SHIP_TO involved party is screened against sanctioned country list configured in GTM. For c: Transaction line item / components Country of Origin = US along with SHIP_TO is screened. For d: Transaction line containing iron & steel item / components entering Europe (SHIP_FROM outside Europe, SHIP_TO within Europe) will be sanctioned. This will require manually review by the Trade compliance team to resolve. - TS_SANCTION_COUNTRIES_PASSED/ TS_SANCTION_COUNTRIES_FAILED will be status according to the screening result for the transaction line. Product classification Process
- Product classification look up would happen from item Master
- TS_Product_classification status would be updated to TS_Product_classification_complete or TS_Product_classification_incomplete or TS_Product_classification_not started
When trade transaction has RPLS, Sanction and Product classification has status TS_RPLS_PASSED & TS_SANCTION_COUNTRIES_PASSED and TS_PRODUCT_CLASSIFICATION_COMPLETE response is sent automatically. In case of failure of trade transaction, the response is sent manually by Trade compliance team and the shipment has to be put on Hold.

## Purpose

This Design Specification documents the detailed design updating ABC Classification on a given Item. This document describes the functional design of the process to generate the ABC Classification for the Items and then update the same at Item level. ## Overview and Scope

Overview
Business Purpose
The Purpose of this integration is to assign Classification to Items based on which they will be cyclically counted and adjusted to maintain Inventory Accuracy. Scope
Scope is limited to copying Classification to Item Master. Scope does not include the Logic for generating Item classification. Return to Vendor process is not in scope of this document,
Functional Overview
- The frequency with which Items are counted your items depends upon the criticality of the item. Oracle Inventory fusion provides a feature to execute ABC Analysis based on the Onhand Stock of Items. The ABC analysis divides an inventory into different categories- "A items", "B items", "C items" , "D items" Varying in from very tightly control and accurate records to less tightly controlled and minimal records. Once the analysis is Run, an ABC Assignment Group is created with Details of Items in each Group. - A new Process will be created which will lookup the Items in the assignment group and updated the corresponding class in the Item Master EFF. # Business Objectives

The Objective is to enable ABC Classification Information generated in Fusion to be made available in WMS for Cycle Counting to be executed.

# Introduction

## Purpose

This Design Specification documents the detailed design for items Cost Interface from Fusion to Oracle Cloud WMS. This document describes the functional design of the list of attributes which need to be interfaced from Fusion to Cloud WMS through Oracle Integrated Cloud Service (OIC) to update Item Cost (Cost Element – Material) in WMS. The design document also covers the event attribute mappings from Fusion to Oracle Cloud WMS Functional Columns. ## Overview and Scope

Overview
For performing Cycle Count transactions in WMS, item cost data is required. Since item cost is required in WMS for the Cycle Count approvals, synchronization service will be needed to send the create / update Cost information to Cloud WMS. Business Purpose
Cycle Counting will be done in Oracle Cloud WMS. For the Cycle Count approvals, the Item Standard Cost is required to trigger the approvals based on the Tolerance percentages set at Cycle Count level. Hence, a specific interface needs to be built between Fusion and Cloud WMS as per the Business Requirement to keep item cost data in sync between the two systems. This design document focuses on building an interface between Fusion and Cloud WMS so that item cost data can be kept in sync. Scope
The scope of this document is limited to functional design of the interface to communicate items’ standard cost additions and updates from Fusion to Cloud WMS System. Functional Overview
Fusion Cost Management is a source for all item cost information.

As such, it is a master repository to hold all cost data, which is defined at Item number and inventory organization level. Product Cost information is published to consuming systems with their related entities for downstream consumption, as per configured publication criteria, to determine what data elements (Item Attributes) get published to what systems and at what cadence. Fusion Cost Management will publish only the items and its cost that meet the publication criteria in the Cost Management for the WMS downstream system. Standard Cost of all the items that need to be cycle counted in the warehouses needs to be interfaced into the Item master in WMS. Standard Cost is maintained under different Cost Scenarios in Cost Accounting Work Area under Inventory Management. Only the Published Cost Scenarios’ data (Unit Cost of Cost Element - Material) of the Cost Organizations of [Anonymized Customer] (now) and UK (in future) needs to be pushed from Fusion to WMS. There can be 2 approaches for the Integration:
- The Integration can be event-based with point-to-point integration. While user runs the Update Standard Cost program for the selected Cost Scenario, system can push all the Items in the Cost Scenario along with its Cost details from Fusion to WMS
- The Integration can be batch-based program, which runs every 1 hour and will send the Cost data in Published status in the last 1 hour (from the previous run) from Fusion to WMS
The Cost Master should include the following details at minimum:
- Item Number
- Valuation Unit
- Status (Published)
- Effective Start Date
- Unit Cost (Cost Element – Material)
By integrating Fusion Item Cost Master to WMS, all the item’s Material cost details, as listed above, are expected to be integrated into WMS, which will help in processing the Cycle Count approvals accurately. With reference to storing the Cost in WMS, it has to be stored against the Item and Company combination. There needs to be a mapping between the Valuation Unit (Fusion) and Company code (WMS) maintained in order to store the Item Cost at Company level. # Business Objectives

The Cost Management (Cost Master) maintains master cost information enabling an enterprise to link all its critical cost data to one source, providing a common point of reference.

As part of the business process, costs need to be published from Cost Management to the Warehouse Management System (WMS). The integration solution is designed to enable scalable integrations to accommodate future requirements. The following objectives were captured during the Focus Stage and are addressed by the functional designs described in this document:

# Introduction

## Purpose

The objective of this document is to provide a Technical Specification to:
Establish a functional design to address key business objectives. Provide traceability between business requirements and the delivered components. Identify the touchpoints for any functional level integration. Capture any key dependencies. Provide high level functional design for [Anonymized Customer] ERP Leads and Technical Leads to confirm what will be delivered. Provide the necessary information with enough detail so that the technical teams, and/or external 3rd parties, have a clear understanding of the functional requirements that will enable them to design and build the extension component to satisfy the requirements. Assist the testing teams in understanding what to test. ## Scope

This document specifies the business context, requirements, dependencies, and technical considerations for the technical team for the development & configuration for CR055- Create automatic Document Structure Templates for item classes. ## Overview

[Anonymized Customer] will maintain Its Key documentation by using Document objects in PLM. Document structure will be created under a parent document folder. The folder takes its unique identifier name from the part / item it relates to - Typically Doc-012345. This parent folder is in turn then related to the item. However, it relies on individuals setting up folder structures for each new item manually - Users will need to be carefully trained, to ensure Standardised folder structure and naming conventions. From this standardisation and harmonisation comes governance benefits - from ease of searching, expiry dates for folders and or documents, efficiency in one document to many parts scenarios like electronic component data and compliance sheets, etc. etc.

# Business Objectives

## Process Overview

Create a template based on item class to auto populate a consistent file folder structure for each new item. This template would create the structure and name each folder of document object. This would save considerable time for users / engineers, it would give a clean, repeatable doc structure leading to a global standard. (A key aspiration of the Novus project) And eliminate naming convention / part number issues. ## Business Requirements

Create automatic Document Structure Templates for specific item classes. Several document structures would exist for common item classes that require specification, quality and compliance data / evidence. Structure example:
As standard, templates do not exist for document objects. An extension would be required as follows:
Once an Item is created (in this example Item created = EPT-206371) a business event would fire to initiate the Integration Orchestration in OIC. The Integration process flow:

- The Document Child items will be created as follows using above example:

### Assumptions

The following key assumptions are required to support this design. - All Document Objects Parent and Child, Item Numbers will start with the prefix ‘DST-’. - Prior to Technical Build, the following items will be provided:
- Confirm structure mapping as outlined in the mapping spreadsheet provided. - All applicable Leaf Level ICCs defined and configured in the development environment. - Not all ICC’s will require a document structure. If upon Item Creation the ICC is not found in the document structure mapping, end the process. - The item structure rules will be limited, e.g., 5 structures for common item classes (ICC’s) that require specification, quality, and compliance data/evidence. - Any exceptions, e.g., a new document object, could be added manually via the UI’s after the pre-defined document structure has been created. - When Document Items are created the business event will fire again, so the OIC orchestration needs to consider how to ignore these, e.g. Document Items will be assigned an Item Class ‘Externally Supplied Document’.

Whatever mechanism is chosen it needs to consider that more Document Objects may be added in the future. - Mapping table will be maintained in ATP:
- This CR (integration components) can only be deployed after items have been migrated to any instance. Otherwise, it will cause issues with bulk load because business events will be fired for each individual item load and subsequent APIs called via orchestration to create the document objects. It has been highlighted in the requirement gathering meetings for this CR that [Anonymized Customer] activities will need to create document structures (manual or automated) for existing items migrated as a separate activity. ### High Level Approach

- Integration “XxScmExtractItemsforDICreation” will be a scheduled integration which will extract Items with specific criteria using Fusion Custom BIP Report  Xx_Erp_Create_Document_Items_for_NewItems
- Items created with Item Class mentioned in ICCLeafValue of Mapping document, life cycle status as “Priliminary” and Item Status as “Inactive’ are picked. - XxScmExtractItemsforDICreation will verify if the item picked have Item Relationship with type “Document” is created or not. Eg. For Item “ESW100001” , OIC will check if “DST- ESW100001” is attached to  “ESW100001” as Related item of type “Document”. If relationship doesn’t exist, It will invoke “InvokeXxScmCreateDocItems” internal integration with parameters, Item Number and Item Class. - Mapping table in prior section “xxdom_doc_structure_lookup.csv” is maintained in ATP table
- InvokeXxScmCreateDocItems function is to create document parent item, create child items using mapping table, create item structure and create item relationship. - Invoke Integration shall check if any item with parameter Item Number prefixed with “DST-” already exist. It will create Document Parent Item. - Invoke Integration will then get list of Child Item’s and its corresponding Item class to be created from ATP database. It will check if any items already exists with child item number already in system and then create the child items. - Once all Document Parent and Child items are created, Item Structure is created for Document Parent Item with all of its Document Child Items. - As final step, Integration will create Item Relationship with type “Document” between Parameter Item Number and Document Parent Item Number
- OIC, shall send the notification email specific users mentioned in common lookup in case of any errors.

### Integrations

- ERP Warranty Extension
Activity Details:
The integration will be scheduled to run once a day. GetLookup_ERP_Invoke: This will fetch the customer that is setup in the lookup XX_DOM_ADDL_WARR. ### Functional Requirement

ATO Models are within a PTO model structure and when the order is placed, it generates an error in the Supply Chain Financial Orchestration:
The business event could not be processed because attribute UnitPrice is invalid. (FOS-3465136)
For ATO Model ordered within PTO model Structure, Supply Chain Financial Orchestration is not creating Intercompany Transaction Event due to Unit Price being null in interfaced event as a part of Shipment Transaction. This is happening due to Rollup flag in Sales Order is not set for ATO Model if ordered under PTO Hybrid Model. This integration will publish Unit Price as 0 for the Financial Orchestration lines and re-trigger the Financial Orchestration Events. ### Functional Configuration

# Functional Overview

### Functional Requirement

[Anonymized Customer] Planners need the information on the Expected Receipt date of the ordered (PO) items from Suppliers to plan for the manufacturing of the printers and other finished products. This is an essential information which is required to plan better. Currently, while the ASN is created against the Purchase Order, system does not update the Shipment Method as available in the Purchase Order automatically and does not calculate the Expected Receipt Date based on the Shipment Method chosen by the user while creating ASN. Instead, it calculates the Expected Receipt Date based on the Default Shipment Method as available for the Supplier Site and Inventory Location combination as part of the Transit Times setup. This design document focuses on building an integration to update the Shipment Method in the ASN as available in the Purchase Order and to calculate the Expected Receipt Date as per the Shipment Method selected in the ASN. Scope
The scope of this CR is as follows:
- Introduction of a Header level DFFs in Redwood ASN page to capture the Shipping Method and Shipping Date (while Expected Receipt Date is calculated and updated in ASN), to use to it for comparison with the selected Shipping Method and Shipping Date in ASN.

- Develop a custom BIP Report to extract the eligible ASNs along with Shipment Method, Shipping Date and Expected Receipt Date
- OIC Integration development to update Shipping Method, Expected Receipt and DFFs in ASN (both creation and modification), using existing Rest APIs including logic to considering Receiving Calendars and Organization calendars from Transportation Schedules and Inventory Organizations setups. ### Functional Configuration

### Functional Requirement

For assets Ship To party name in the Customer fields, but Account number belongs to Bill To Party, we are unable to create Debriefs against such assets. In case of different Bill To and Ship To parties, the system expects Bill To party to be stamped in the Customer field. But at [Anonymized Customer], they are trained to attach the Ship To party in Customer field. Now even if they are re-trained mistakes can happen. So, we need to make sure asset is created with Bill To party in asset’s Customer field irrespective of what party user chooses on Order Header’s Customer Field To achieve this, we pause the orchestration process in appropriate stages and release the same based on the task completion status. ### Functional Configuration

### High Level Approach

Following is the High Level flow:
- WMS calls a Fusion ESS job to get the output of a BIP Report to pick all the Transfer Order lines which have errored out as part the cancellations as they were interfaced to WMS
- Lock would be applied on the related Order in WMS
- In WMS, for the Orders that where locked successfully, further call is made to Fusion integration by WMS to:
- Update the Interface status in Fusion from “Interfaced” to “Ready to Interface”
- Backorder and Cancel the Transfer Order line in Fusion

### Pre-Requisites

The following are the prerequisite:
- For running the Get Transfer Order Details Report:
- User needs to have Reports & Analytics functionality enabled to navigate. ### Report Considerations

- Transfer Order line status lookup should be OPEN. - Transfer Order line Interface Error Message Code should be INV_IMT_INTERFACE_ERROR. - Transfer Order line Source Type Lookup should be INV and BACKTOBACK. - Shipping Line Source Line Type should be TRANSFER_ORDER. - Shipping Line WMS Interfaced Flag should be INTERFACED. - Integrated System Code should be ORA_RCS_IS_WMS.

### Assumptions

- For end-to-end flow, connections of the Integration should be in place. - In case of any success/error in the integration, a notification email will be sent to the mail list configured in the OIC lookup. ### High Level Approach

- This is a scheduled integration which runs every minute
- OIC invokes the BIP report to fetch all the configured items created during that period in fusion
- OIC then calls the REST API to fetch the required details of the configured item
- In the next step OIC calls the REST API to update the Item Weight in Fusion

# Introduction

## Purpose

This Design Specification documents the detailed design for items Interface from Fusion to Oracle Cloud WMS. This document describes the functional design of the list of attributes which need to be interfaced from Fusion to Cloud WMS through Oracle Integrated Cloud Service (OIC) to create items in WMS. The design document also covers the event attribute mappings from Fusion to Oracle Cloud WMS Functional Columns. ## Overview and Scope

Overview
For performing transactions, item data is required in Cloud WMS System. Since items would be created directly in Fusion PDH and synchronization service will need to send the create/ update/ delete information to Cloud WMS. Business Purpose
Items will be created in Oracle PDH; however, the warehouse activities will be carried out for all the manufacturing facilities (enabled as inventory organizations in WMS) using Cloud WMS. Hence, a specific interface needs to be built between Fusion and Cloud WMS as per the Business Requirement to keep item data in sync between the two systems. This design document focuses on building an interface between Fusion and Cloud WMS so that item data can be kept in sync. Scope
The scope of this document is limited to functional design of the interface to communicate items master data additions and updates from Fusion to Cloud WMS System. Functional Overview
Fusion Product Data Hub is a source for all item (product) information.

source_file: wms-docxDOM_INT001_Items Interface from Fusion to WMS_Integrationv1.4.docx.txt
chunk:
As such, it is a master repository to hold all data, which is defined as a product by the Item number, Item description for the Inventory Organizations it is associated with. Product information are published to multiple consuming systems with their related entities for downstream consumption, as per configured publication criteria, to determine what data elements (Item Attributes) get published to what systems and at what cadence. Fusion Product Hub will publish only the products that meet the publication criteria in the PDH for the WMS downstream systems in respect of New Items and or Change order. All the items that need to be received and shipped out of the warehouses needs to be interfaced into the Item master in WMS. The PDH Item Master should include the following details at minimum:
- Item Number
- Item Description
- Unit Length
- Unit Width
- Unit Height
- Unit Weight
- Unit Volume
Item attribute tracked (Y/N) QC Required (Attribute)
Item attribute Country of Origin
Item Serial No tracked (Y/N)
Item Expiry controlled tracked (Y/N) (If so product life & % Acceptable)
Item batch no tracked (Y/N)
Velocity Code (ABC classification)
The integration will be event-based with point-to-point integration. By integrating Fusion Product Master (including the required Org level items) to WMS, all the item’s details, attributes and relationships, as listed above, are expected to be integrated into WMS, which will help in processing the inbound and outbound orders accurately. Outside PLM, Oracle Inventory Cloud (INV) will also be required to provide the ABC classifications for items to WMS. ABC classification is maintained at inventory organisation level. ABC classification will be added in EFF in item from where the integration will pick ABC classification and send it to WMS in the item field velocity code. # Business Objectives

The Product Hub (Item Master) maintains master item information enabling an enterprise to link all its critical item data to one source, providing a common point of reference. As part of the business process, items need to be published from Fusion Product Hub to the Warehouse Management System (WMS). The integration solution is designed to enable scalable integrations to accommodate future requirements.

# Introduction

## Purpose

This Design Specification documents the detailed design for Supplier Interface from Fusion to Oracle Cloud WMS. This document describes the functional design of the list of attributes which need to be interfaced from Fusion to Cloud WMS through Oracle Integrated Cloud Service (OIC) to create suppliers in WMS. The design document also covers the event attribute mappings from Fusion to Oracle Cloud WMS Functional Columns. ## Overview and Scope

Overview
For creating PO receipts, supplier data is required in Cloud WMS System. Since suppliers would be created directly in Fusion and synchronization service will need to send the create/ update information to Cloud WMS. Business Purpose
All Purchasing transactions will be recorded in Oracle Cloud ERP, however the warehouse activities will be carried out for all the manufacturing facilities (inventory organization enabled in WMS) using Cloud WMS. Both the systems need to communicate to complete the Receiving part of the Procure to Pay cycle for every single procurement transaction. Requisitions, Purchase orders will be primarily recorded in Oracle Procurement Cloud. Actual Receipts would be recorded in Cloud WMS upon receiving the Receipt Advice. However, to enable this receiving part of the procure to pay cycle, supplier data in Cloud WMS needs to be in sync with Fusion. WMS will be the material transaction system and Fusion will be the operational system (system of records). Hence, a specific interface needs to be built between Fusion and Cloud WMS as per the Business Requirement to keep Supplier data in sync between the two systems. This design document focuses on building an interface between Fusion and Cloud WMS so that Supplier data can be kept in sync.

# Introduction

## Purpose

The objective of this document is to provide a Design Specification for Inventory transaction and inventory reconciliation between WMS and Fusion cloud. - Also, to provide the necessary information with enough detail so that the Project team, have a clear understanding of the design and functional requirements. ## Scope

This document specifies the business context, functional requirements, and details to integrate different inventory transactions happening in WMS Cloud (cycle count, sub inventory transfer, stock write off) and the inventory balance snapshot from WMS to Fusion cloud. A warehouse management system (or WMS) is a software application designed to support warehouse or distribution center management and staff. They facilitate management of available resources to move and store materials into, within, and out of a warehouse, while supporting staff in material movement and storage. Inventory Management Cloud supports a central integration framework across Oracle Procurement Cloud, Oracle Order Management Cloud, and Oracle Inventory Management based on web services to support the interactions between WMS and Fusion Cloud. ## Functional Overview

Fusion Inventory Management supports a central integration framework for working with warehouse management systems (WMS). The inventory management suite of products includes Fusion Receiving, Fusion Inventory Management, and Fusion Shipping. All the inventory adjustment transactions performed in WMS should be interfaced to Oracle inventory to update the on-hand quantities as well as track the transactions. The Functional Specifications described here below refers to the integration scenario of inventory adjustment performed in WMS.

- Cycle Count Adjustment
In Fusion, the items will be classified under different count classes (ABC Classification) based on a certain criterion. The items would then be updated in WMS and the cycle count process for those classes will be carried out in WMS. The adjustments would then be posted to Fusion with the transaction type as WMS Cycle Count Receipt or WMS Cycle Count Issue and the transaction source type will be Inventory. This section of the integration between WMS and Inventory Cloud has the purpose to cover the Inventory adjustments when Cycle count is performed in WMS. Cycle count can be performed for both Reserve and Active locations. Cycle count can be done at LPN level (CC Location LPN Scan-Scan the location and each LPN in the location) Or at LPN Detail level (CC Location Content- Scan the location and each LPN in the location, followed by the SKU quantity) or Cycle Count Active Location (Scan the location-Scan SKU-Scan Item-Enter Quantity-Scan serial/lot). Inventory history record will get created after performing Cycle count. Inventory history record will contain respective Inventory History Activity Codes with Original and Adjusted quantity.

This document specifies the business context, functional requirements, and details to integrate Oracle Fusion Purchase Order from Procurement to Oracle Cloud WMS for Receipt transactions. A warehouse management system (or WMS) is a software application designed to support warehouse or distribution center management and staff. They facilitate management of available resources to move and store materials into, within, and out of a warehouse, while supporting staff in material movement and storage. Coordinating the communication with these systems to support purchase order receipts, returns to vendors, internal material transfers, inventory transactions, and sales order shipments is a substantial integration effort. Inventory Management Cloud supports a central integration framework across Oracle Procurement Cloud, Oracle Order Management Cloud, and Oracle Inventory Management based on web services to support the interactions between WMS and Fusion Cloud. Using these services, Inventory Management Cloud communicates Receipt Advice to Oracle Cloud WMS for processing. ## Functional Overview

Purchase Orders are created and approved in Fusion Procurement, as soon they are approved, orders are interfaced to WMS by ESS job ‘Generate Receipt Advice’ Program. In WMS, Purchase Orders are referred during receiving process in WMS.

Allows for below transactions:
- Creation
- Modification (until receipt in initiated in WMS)

# Business Objectives

The details such as PO number, supplier information, item number, item revision & quantity are published to WMS. In WMS, warehouse employee is responsible in performing below operations:

- Put Away of material in specified facility along with additional details of Locator/Serials/Lot if any. ## Process Overview

### Assumptions

It only covers create/ update operation. - In case of any success/error in the integration, a notification email will be sent to the mail list configured in the OIC lookup. - Draft purchase orders and purchase order revisions are not taken into consideration. - The “Generate Receipt Advice” program will be scheduled, so it should not be submitted manually by user unless in case of urgency. ### High Level Approach

- The integration will trigger once the ESS job – “Generate Receipt Advice” is submitted. Integration will be subscribing to the event for “Receipt Advice Event Notification”. - “Generate Receipt Advice” job will be scheduled in fusion as per frequency decided to extract the purchase order details created after the last successful run of job. - Integration will be triggered by subscribing the event Business event “Receipt Advice Event Notification” is applied in the source ERP adapter responsible for the invocation of OIC integration. - The payload received from SCM will contains the purchase order details and purchase order line details.

- The payload will be then converted into WMS XML required format by invoking the Rest API echoLgfDataOrder which will do the XML transformation internally. - The transformed XML data will be interfaced to WMS cloud using WMS InitStageInterfaceAPI service. ### Pre-Requisites

This document specifies the business context, functional requirements, and details to integrate Oracle Fusion to Oracle Cloud WMS for Return Material Authorization Orders interfaced as ASNs with the ASN type as “RMA”. A warehouse management system (or WMS) is a software application designed to support warehouse or distribution center management and staff. They facilitate management of available resources to move and store materials into, within, and out of a warehouse, while supporting staff in material movement and storage. Coordinating the communication with these systems to support purchase order receipts, returns to vendors, internal material transfers, inventory transactions, and sales order shipments is a substantial integration effort. Inventory Management Cloud supports a central integration framework across Oracle Procurement Cloud, Oracle Order Management Cloud, and Oracle Inventory Management based on web services to support the interactions between WMS and Fusion Cloud. Using these services, Inventory Management Cloud communicates Receipt Advice to Oracle Cloud WMS for processing. ## Functional Overview

# Business Objectives

When integrating Oracle Inventory Management Cloud with a warehouse management system (or WMS), there is the requirement to send the RMA information as Receipt Advice to allow the Receiving Inventory Organization in WMS to Receive and Put away the RMA stock. RMA Business Flow:
The above picture depicts the general steps in the Return Material Authorization (RMA) business flow. The steps initiate in Fusion Order Management with the creation of the RMA. This RMA is then interfaced to WMS via OIC integration to create an Inbound Shipment. In WMS the user receives the requested items and locates them into a put away location. The receipt information along with the put away are then interfaced back to Fusion to update the ASN and adjust the inventory stock quantities to reflect the received quantity. The Generate Receipt Advice from Inventory to WMS will push the RMAs to WMS for further execution in WMS. The details such as RMA (ASN) number, as item number, return quantity, return order, and return to warehouse etc. are get published to WMS. In WMS, warehouse employee is responsible in performing below operations:
- Creation of Receipt
- Put Away of material in specified return facility along with additional details of Locator/Serials/Lot if any. Once Put Away is performed in WMS, the item is physically returned into warehouse. An inventory person will now send receipt confirmation details (detailed put away material transaction) to Inventory and same is responsible in progressing the return sales order to Credit the [Anonymized Customer] or closure without credit. ## Process Overview

- Create RMA in Fusion Order Management. - Schedule the process in Oracle Inventory Management “Generate Receipt Advice”. The scheduled process Generate Receipt Advice publishes an event to notify the WMS that receipt advice is ready to be interfaced. The web service Send Receipt Advice provides the ability for the WMS to receive the actual receipt advice with the expected shipment lines for Return Material Authorization (RMAs). - After the WMS receives the receipt advice for RMA, an ASN gets created with details like [Anonymized Customer] Name, return quantity etc. from return order and performs receiving-related processes including receiving and put away.

## Scope

This document specifies the business context, functional requirements, and details to integrate the receipt and delivery transactions performed using PO/ASN/RMA in Oracle Cloud WMS to Oracle Fusion Inventory. A warehouse management system (or WMS) is a software application designed to support warehouse or distribution center management and staff. They facilitate management of available resources to move and store materials into, within, and out of a warehouse, while supporting staff in material movement and storage. Inventory Management Cloud supports a central integration framework across Oracle Procurement Cloud, Oracle Order Management Cloud, and Oracle Inventory Management based on web services to support the interactions between WMS and Fusion Cloud. Using these services, Inventory Management Cloud communicates Receipt Advice to Oracle Cloud WMS for processing. ## Functional Overview

Purchase Orders/Advance Shipment Notification/Return Material Authorization documents are created and approved in Oracle Fusion, as soon they are approved, orders are interfaced to WMS by ESS job ‘Generate Receipt Advice’ Program.

In WMS, Purchase Orders/Advance Shipment Notification/Return Material Authorization are referred during receiving process in WMS, and further delivery transaction is performed in WMS. # Business Objectives

When integrating Oracle Inventory Management Cloud with a warehouse management system (or WMS), there is the requirement to send the Purchase Order/ASN/RMA Information as Receipt Advice to allow the Receiving Inventory Organization in WMS to Receive and Putaway the stock. The Generate Receipt Advice from Inventory to WMS will push the PO/ASN/RMA to WMS for further execution in WMS. The details such as PO number, supplier information, item number, item revision & quantity are published to WMS. In WMS, warehouse employee is responsible in performing below operations:
- Creation of Receipt
- Put Away of material in specified facility along with additional details of Locator/Serials/Lot if any. Direct delivery of the PRODUKTION stock will be performed to the lineside locations based on the puta way rules configured in WMS. The same information will be triggered to Fusion along with the locator updates. Since the PRODUKTION stock is only maintained in Fusion, the OIC will trigger an additional request to WMS to decrement the PRODUKTION stock in WMS after the put away transaction is completed. ## Process Overview

The Functional Specifications described here below refers to the integration scenario of Receipt Confirmation performed through an ASN which is outbound from WMS and inbound to SCM Cloud. The solution designed in this document is that allows to bring ‘delivered’ stock information from WMS to SCM Cloud application. Item code

Purchase Order Number

# Introduction

## Purpose

The objective of this document is to provide a Design Specification to:
Provide the necessary information with enough detail so that the Project team, have a clear understanding of the design and functional requirements. ## Scope

This document specifies the business context, functional requirements, and details to integrate Oracle Fusion to Oracle Cloud WMS for Sales Order Shipping Process. A warehouse management system (or WMS) is a software application designed to support warehouse or distribution center management and staff. They facilitate management of available resources to move and store materials into, within, and out of a warehouse, while supporting staff in material movement and storage. Coordinating the communication with these systems to support purchase order receipts, returns to vendors, internal material transfers, inventory transactions, and sales order shipments is a substantial integration effort. Inventory Management Cloud supports a central integration framework across Oracle Procurement Cloud, Oracle Order Management Cloud, and Oracle Inventory Management based on web services to support the interactions between WMS and Fusion Cloud. Using these services, Inventory Management Cloud communicates Sales Order shipment request to Oracle Cloud WMS for processing. ## Functional Overview

[Anonymized Customer] business process flow requires the Sales Order to be created and configured in Order Management system. Once the Sales Order is created it should be interfaced to the WMS for the further processing. The Sales Order integration between Fusion and WMS will run every 10 Minutes and pick all the sales order lines which are Awaiting Shipment and are not already interfaced to WMS.

# Business Objectives

When integrating Oracle Inventory Management Cloud with a warehouse management system (or WMS), there is a requirement to send the sales order created in Fusion to WMS so that further processes can be performed in WMS system to ship the Sales Order. Business Flow:
The above picture depicts the process flow as per business requirement. The sales order is created and configured in Fusion Order Management. The Sales Order line(s) goes to GTM for trade screening once the order is successfully screened then manufacturing work order is created for the configured item(s). After completion of the Work order the Sales Order lines Wait for Shipment. At this moment an integration will trigger between Fusion Inv and WMS to interface the Sales Order lines to WMS. The above picture depicts the general steps in the Sales order business flow. The steps initiate in Fusion Order Management with the creation of a Sales Order. This sales order gets interfaced to WMS via OIC integration to create an Outbound Order. WMS allocates the order and ship it. The shipment details are then interfaced back to Fusion to update the shipment information, decrement the inventory quantities in stock and to update the sales order status. Each Shipping line will create a separate Order in WMS. The Sales Order Number column will reference the Fusion order with an additional sequence number except for the shipset orders. Shipset orders will have multiple order lines for the same order. The orders will be interfaced to WMS with a Delivery ID. The delivery ID is generated based on the shipping method, ship to country, scheduled ship date and the customer party site number. ## Process Overview

- Create the Sales Order with the Configured item. - Sales Order lines reach to Awaiting Shipping. - Generate Shipment Request ESS job runs. - All the Sales Order lines which are not already interfaced will be interfaced to WMS (INT007.) - A new WMS Sales Order will be created based on the data provided by Fusion. # Pre-Conditions

- Shipment line should not be already interfaced to WMS. - Shipment line should be in the Awaiting Shipping status.

### Assumptions

- This interface between SCM and WMS Cloud for shipment requests covers Sales Orders with no previously reserved lines, sales orders with existing reservations on specific lots (aka de-stocking orders) and transfer orders. - This integration does not cover “Return Transfer Orders”, which correspond to shipments needed because of material received from other organizations or facilities through a Transfer Order that now needs to be returned. - This integration will not take in consideration lines which have been manually assigned to a Shipment in SCM Cloud. It is WMS role to execute shipments so shipments should not be created in SCM Cloud for WMS controlled organizations. - This integration will take in consideration lines for inventory items only. Orders for services or recurring charges, etc. which do not use inventory items will not be taken in consideration. - Draft sales orders and sales order revisions are not taken in consideration. - In general, the integration will depend on Release Rules defined in Inventory.

What is excluded from the Release Rule will not be considered. However, it is possible to have one or more schedules of “Generate Shipment Requests” using different Release Rules. - The “Generate Shipment Request” program will be scheduled, so it should not be submitted manually by user unless in case of urgency (e.g. missing orders, wrong orders, urgent shipment requests, etc.). ### High Level Approach

- The integration will trigger once the ESS job – “Generate Shipment Request” is submitted. Integration will be subscribing to the event for “Generate Shipment Request”. - “Generate Shipment Request” job will be scheduled in fusion as per frequency decided to extract the sales order details created after the last successful run of job. - Integration will be triggered by subscribing the event Business event ‘Generate Shipment Requests’ is applied in the source ERP adapter responsible for the invocation of OIC integration. - The payload received from contains from SCM will contains the shipment order details and shipment line details. - The payload will be then converted into WMS XML required format using stage Write operation which will do the XML transformation internally. - The transformed XML data will be interfaced to WMS cloud using WMS InitStageInterfaceAPI service. ### Pre-Requisites

A warehouse management system (or WMS) is a software application designed to support warehouse or distribution center management and staff. They facilitate management of available resources to move and store materials into, within, and out of a warehouse, while supporting staff in material movement and storage. Coordinating the communication with these systems to support purchase order receipts, returns to vendors, internal material transfers, inventory transactions, and sales order shipments is a substantial integration effort. Inventory Management Cloud supports a central integration framework across Oracle Procurement Cloud, Oracle Order Management Cloud, and Oracle Inventory Management based on web services to support the interactions between WMS and Fusion Cloud. Using these services, Inventory Management Cloud communicates Sales Order shipment request to Oracle Cloud WMS for processing. ## Functional Overview

[Anonymized Customer] business process flow requires WMS to send the Shipment Confirmation notification to Oracle Fusion on successfully shipping the sales order in WMS. On receiving the request Shipment Lines of the Sales Order in Fusion should get marked as Shipped to complete the fulfillment process in Fusion. This integration will run as in when an order is shipped in WMS.

Sales order or transfer order documents are created in Oracle fusion cloud. Order orchestration steps take the orders to awaiting shipping and then order will be eligible to interface to WMS cloud. The delivery ID is generated based on the customer ship to name, ship to country, scheduled ship date and the customer party site number. Order will be interfaced to WMS and Delivery Id will be a sent as Externally planned load number on the WMS Order lines. Orders will be waved for allocation and task creation. Task will be performed and pick pack will be completed. Load will be shipped from WMS Cloud. This will interface the shipping details to Fusion Inventory cloud to ship confirm the delivery. # Business Objectives

When integrating Oracle Warehouse Management system (or WMS) with Oracle Inventory Management Cloud, there is a requirement to send the Ship Confirmation request of WMS to Fusion Oracle Inventory Management so that Sales Order lines in fusion can be marked as Shipped. Business Flow:
The above picture depicts the process flow as per business requirement. Fusion sales order is interfaced to WMS and a new Sales Order is created in WMS. This sales order will further get Pick, Pack and Ship in WMS. Once a sales order is shipped, Shipment Confirmation integration will be triggered from WMS to Oracle Fusion to notify the Fusion system that the sales order is shipped. On receiving the Shipment Confirmation request from WMS, Sales Order line status will be changed from Awaiting Shipping to Shipped to mark the end of fulfillment. The above picture depicts the general steps in the Sales order business flow. The steps initiate in Fusion Order Management with the creation of a Sales Order. This sales order gets interfaced to WMS via OIC integration to create an Outbound Order. WMS allocates the order and ship it. The shipment details are then interfaced back to Fusion to update the shipment information, decrement the inventory quantities in stock and to update the sales order status. ## Process Overview

- The scheduled process Generate Shipment Request enables inventory management users to send shipment lines to the WMS using the task Create Outbound Shipment request using a scheduled process. - Delivery Id will be created by grouping the order by customer, ship to address and schedule ship date. Order will be interfaced to WMS and Delivery Id will be a sent as External plan load number on the WMS Order lines.

- After the all the lines in the delivery/load is picked and packed and loading operation will be performed using RF transactions. - Before ship load Waybill no, Shipping charges will be entered on the Obload. In case of the ship method change other than what is there on the sales order, it can be updated by changing ship method on carrier field on Obload screen. - Load will be shipped from WMS Cloud. The Receive Shipment Confirmation is new web service when initiated with the required input, receives and processes the shipment confirmation messages. This service interprets and transforms the message and creates the necessary records in the shipping open interface tables. This transformation provides the mechanism for the WMS to send the material and shipping details for the shipment lines fulfilled. - The scheduled process Perform Shipping Transactions processes the pending transaction records received into the open interface tables. The process validates the data on the transaction records received from the WMS before processing them. Any errors from the validation step are recorded, and the transaction records remain in the open interface tables. The interface records with errors are available for users to view, edit, or resolve the errors, or reprocess. The following is a high-level view of the most relevant information to be considered:
Facility Code (Inventory Organization in SCM Cloud)
Company Code (Business Unit in SCM Cloud)
Order Number
Shipment line number
Item code
Load number (Mapped to Delivery/shipment number)
Packed Quantity
Lock code (Mapped to Sub inventory in SCM Cloud)
Serial Number
Lot Number
Weight
Volume
Freight cost
Carrier
Waybill no

# Introduction

## Purpose

The objective of this document is to provide a Design Specification to:
Provide the necessary information with enough detail so that the Project team, have a clear understanding of the design and functional requirements. ## Scope

This document specifies the business context, functional requirements, and details to integrate Oracle Fusion to Oracle Cloud WMS for Sales Order change management process. A warehouse management system (or WMS) is a software application designed to support warehouse or distribution center management and staff. They facilitate management of available resources to move and store materials into, within, and out of a warehouse, while supporting staff in material movement and storage. Coordinating the communication with these systems to support purchase order receipts, returns to vendors, internal material transfers, inventory transactions, and sales order shipments is a substantial integration effort. Inventory Management Cloud supports a central integration framework across Oracle Procurement Cloud, Oracle Order Management Cloud, and Oracle Inventory Management based on web services to support the interactions between WMS and Fusion Cloud. Using these services, Inventory Management Cloud communicates Sales Order changes to Oracle Cloud WMS for processing. ## Functional Overview

[Anonymized Customer] business process flow requires the Change Order to be initiated in Order Management system to facilitate the amendments to the sales order and then the corresponding changes should be performed in WMS system. Once change order is initiated, the integration will first check if the shipment line is already interfaced to WMS or not.

If it’s already interfaced, following steps would be executed via integration:
- Lock the corresponding sales order WMS via integration. - Perform the changes to the sales order in Fusion. - Perform corresponding changes to sales order in WMS via integration. - Unlock the corresponding sales order in WMS via integration. If the shipment line is not already interfaced, the integration will skip the shipment line for processing. # Business Objectives

When integrating Oracle Inventory Management Cloud with a warehouse management system (or WMS), there is the requirement to send the sales order changes in Fusion to WMS so that corresponding changes can be performed in WMS system. Business Flow:
The above picture depicts the process flow as per business requirement. The steps initiate in Fusion Order Management with the creation of the sales order in Fusion order management. This shipment line is interfaced to WMS via shipment request job and corresponding sales order is created in WMS. Based on business need, sales order cancellation/update is initiated in Fusion. The corresponding transaction in WMS is validated if it’s not allocated or picked. If it’s not allocated or picked in WMS, then the corresponding sales order line in fusion is locked. As part of synchronous interface from Fusion to WMS, number lock is applied to corresponding line in WMS. Then the fusion order line is updated. Once changes are completed in Fusion, the corresponding WMS line is updated via synchronous interface from Fusion to WMS. Thereafter, order line in fusion is unlocked. This will trigger unlock operation in WMS line via synchronous integration. This will complete the change order process. ## Process Overview

- Initiate change order process in Fusion Order Management. - Validate the sales order in WMS if it’s not allocated or picked. - Apply lock to the fusion order. - Apply lock to the corresponding WMS order via integration (INT023)
- Perform changes to sales order in Fusion. - Perform changes (updates) to order in WMS via integration (INT022)
- Unlock order in Fusion. - Unlock order in WMS via integration (INT023)

# Pre-Conditions

- Shipment line should be interfaced from Fusion to WMS
- Line in WMS should not be allocated or picked.

# Introduction

## Purpose

This Design Specification documents the detailed design for RTV Interface from Fusion Inventory Management to Oracle Cloud WMS. This document describes the functional design of the list of attributes which need to be interfaced from Fusion to Cloud WMS through Oracle Integrated Cloud Service (OIC) to create RTV Outbound Order in WMS. The design document also covers the event attribute mappings from Fusion to Oracle Cloud WMS Functional Columns. ## Overview and Scope

Overview
All RTV transactions will be recorded first in Fusion. The fields required by Oracle Cloud WMS to carry out the transaction as an Outbound Order shall be queried from Fusion and passed on to OIC wherein the data shall be transformed and mapped to the Sales Order Shipment Outbound Integration from Fusion to Oracle Cloud WMS. This transformed data shall then be sent to WMS to process the RTV transaction as a sales order shipment. The Sales order will be created within WMS with an order type specifically configured for (and as) “RTV”. The sales order would then be waved, picked, packed, and shipped within Oracle Cloud WMS. However, the Shipment Confirmation for such Sales Orders with Order Type “Return to Vendor” will not be sent back to Fusion. Return to Vendor (RTV) transactions will be primarily recorded in Fusion but sent to WMS to adjust the inventory in WMS so, that both the systems are in perfect synchronization. Returns would be created using a 1-way communication from Fusion to Cloud WMS.

# Introduction

## Purpose

This Design Specification documents the detailed design for Movement Request Interface from Fusion to Oracle Cloud WMS. This document describes the functional design of the list of attributes which need to be interfaced from Fusion to Cloud WMS through Oracle Integrated Cloud Service (OIC) to create movement requests in WMS originating from min-max replenishment from Fusion Inventory Management. The design document also covers the event attribute mappings from Fusion to Oracle Cloud WMS Functional Columns. ## Overview and Scope

Overview
Movement requests are requests for the movement of material within an inventory organization such as a warehouse or facility. These types of movement requests exist:
- Replenishment movement requests
- Shop floor movement requests
Business Purpose
Movement Request transaction enables to perform the complete process required to request movement of material, physically move material, and confirm physical movement of material. Hence, a specific interface needs to be built between Fusion and Cloud WMS as per the Business Requirement to keep movement request intact between the two systems. This design document focuses on building an interface between Fusion and Cloud WMS so that movement requests are performed without any issues. Scope
The scope of this document is limited to functional design of the interface movement requests from Fusion to Cloud WMS System. Functional Overview
Fusion Movement Request is a source for all movement requests published to WMS. These movement requests will be interfaced to WMS for different use cases. - Min-Max replenishment process in Fusion will trigger a movement request in WMS to move material to PRODUKTION lineside locations from respective Storage Subinventory specified as part of Min Max Setup at Subinventory Level.

# Introduction

## Purpose

This Design Specification documents details the design for Movement Request pick confirmation interface from Oracle Cloud WMS to Fusion. This document describes the functional design of the list of attributes which need to be interfaced from Oracle Cloud WMS to Fusion through Oracle Integrated Cloud Service (OIC) to pick confirm and close the movement request lines Fusion. The design document also covers the event attribute mappings from Oracle Cloud WMS  to Fusion Functional Columns. ## Overview and Scope

Overview
Movement requests are requests for the movement of material within an inventory organization such as a warehouse or facility. These types of movement requests exist:
- Replenishment movement requests
- Shop floor movement requests
The movement request is then completed (picked and moved) in WMS and this triggers a Pick confirmation record which is communicated back to Fusion inventory to complete the picking action against the Movement request. Business Purpose
Movement Request transaction enables to perform the complete process required to request movement of material, physically move material, and confirm physical movement of material. Hence, a specific interface needs to be built between Oracle Cloud WMS and Fusion as per the Business Requirement to keep movement request intact between the two systems. This design document focuses on building an interface between Oracle Cloud WMS and Fusion so that movement requests are updated without any issues. Scope
The scope of this document is limited to functional design of the interface pick confirmation for movement requests from Oracle Cloud WMS to Fusion. Functional Overview
Fusion Movement Request is a source for all movement requests published to WMS.

- RTV Lineside returns stock to be moved to the RTV sub inventory via the movement request. Movement request would then be pick confirmed in WMS and the triggers the response to Fusion Inventory via OIC. The movement request pick confirmation from WMS (IHT-81 and IHT-91) should include the following details at minimum:
- Movement Request Number (ref_value_3)
- Movement Request Line Number (ref_value_4)
- Movement Request Type (ref_value_5)
Item Code

In Fusion the interface then runs the process “Print Movement Request Pick slip” Report which would create the Pick Slip. While submitting the program, Organization ID and Movement request number are passed as input. Once Pick slip is generated Pick confirmation is done.
